Input: What's the worst experience you've had with telling someone you had feelings for them? While at University I observed that any course that had the word 'Management’ within its name was bound to be laden with beautiful women. When I did Management Accounting I was introduced by Lorna, a good female friend of mine, to this tall, shapely and somewhat quirky young lady with thick black curls, full lips and a shapely body. The only flaw that I observed was she had a slight paunch. Her name was Gabrielle or Gabby as she preferred to be called. She had an outspoken yet aloof disposition whereby she could say the most unfiltered thing and it would never come across offensive, well to me at least. I recall while walking with her and Lorna, Gabby randomly blurted out that my fantasy would be for her and Lorna to carry me to some secret location for a lapdance and ménage à trois. Lorna went red, either in anger, embarassment or a combination of the two. I soon discovered that Gabby's sister attended the school where I worked. I was never able to procure Gabby's phone number as I never got another chance encounter (she was very delinquent in class attendance) and Lorna didn't have it either. I then came up with what I considered a fool proof idea. I would write an old fashioned love letter, explaining my feelings for her and sealed with a kiss I would carry it to her sister to have it delivered to Gabby. All my feelings just flowed out of me as I wrote that long letter. I put a sticker of a rose and then neatly folded it into a red envelope. When I came upon the sister (12 years old at the time) I explained to her my feelings for Gabby and my intention for her to deliver this letter of love to her. I was expecting the sister to gush and swoon (as girls her age are prone to do regarding such romance) but instead she gave me an odd look of confusion and disbelief. 'Are you sure?’ Was all she could reply. 'Yeah,' I said flatly, 'Your sister made such an impression on me. I can't stop thinking of her.’ 'Why don't you just tell her yourself?’ the sister replied in that off-putting, emotionless tone quite strange for a girl her age. 'I don't have her phone number,' I replied and after a brief silence where I'm sure the sister sized me up and decided not to give me Gabby's number, she acquiesced to delivering the letter. The following day, I went up to the sister anxious to hear of what was Gabby's response or better yet collect a letter of my own. 'Did you give her the letter? I asked excitedly. The sister avoided my glances. 'Yeah.' I waited for her response. 'And what happened?’ I said, detecting a faint feeling that this wasn't going to work out well. 'She just looked at it and asked who it was from.’ Another silence. 'And what happened after?’ I said with an underlying sense of dread. 'She asked me what it was you wanted. I told her that you liked her…..she looked at the letter and then put it on her dresser.’ I felt my stomach tighten. 'Didnt she read the letter?’ 'No,' the sister flatly replied, 'She still hasn't opened it.’ There was an awkward silence and the sister then uttered, 'Sir I have to go.’ I felt like the world's biggest clown. I half imagined the sister running to tell a her classmates what a loser Mr. Williamson was and then describing the story. Fast forward four months later and I'm shopping around for car insurance. I head into this big building and none other than Gabby is sitting at the reception office, heavily pregnant. She engages me in delightful quirky conversation as normal almost as though the whole love letter incident was a figment of my imagination. I bid her adieu and immediately called Lorna to tell her what happened to her friend. 'My friend!’ Lorna said shocked, 'She wasn't my friend. She's just a girl from my class. I thought she was your friend! Didn't you realize she was pregnant?’ I replied no and then explained my prior feelings for Gabby and the whole love letter fiasco. 'You sent Gabby a love letter!’ Lorna cried in great shock, 'But she's pregnant….and she's engaged. Didn't you see the ring on her finger?’ Suddenly I just felt like a massive brick landed on my head. Soon the pieces started to fit together.

What "poverty food" is actually really delicious? Trinidad has many types of delicious poverty meals that stem from colonialism, slavery and East Indian indentureship. Some are despondently looked upon with embarassment while others are now expensive delicacies that tourists pay, 'ah pound and ah crown’ for. Poor poverty meals These are the meals that really represent someone going through hard times. These are the delicacies prepared from the remnants of the pantry and hunger induced experimentation. Rice and butter As the name suggests, boiled rice grains soaked in butter. Actually it's not butter but margarine, as real butter here is more expensive than most meats. Exceedingly unhealthy but much more delicious than you would imagine. Just imagine the taste of mashed potatoes except it's rice. Flour porridge Heat some white flour on a skillet and just before it's about to burn throw in some condensed milk and water. This is a Haitian recipe but used by many older Trinis who want to feel full but can't afford to buy groceries. According to how well you garnish this concoction, it can be a hidden delight. Plain egg rice When you have one egg and a bag of rice and you need to feed an entire family, this is the meal of choice. Basically you heat up some boiled rice and throw in a well beaten egg. You will be astonished at how far one egg can stretch. Green fig (banana) with ‘butter’ and salt A family with a couple of banana trees in the yard could be saved from starvation with this simple, delicious meal. Boil a couple full but unripe bananas (with or without skin) and serve with margarine and salt. A fully developed green fig well soaked in margarine with a dash of salt can beat meals in most 5 star restaurants. Banana fritters Instead of throwing away your near rotted bananas, mash them to a pulp, knead in some flour and deep fry in oil. Even when eaten cold these fritters are a treat. Rich Poverty Meals These were meals made from ingredients the upper class and colonial masters would discard such as chickens’ neck and pig's tail. Now they are culinary delights that tourists flock towards and are quite expensive to make/purchase. Chicken Foot souse Don't run away just yet. This flavor will knock your socks off. This is basically boiled chicken's feet soaked in a zesty broth. You'd be surprised the amount of meat a chicken's foot can give. Geera neck Dont throw away those chicken necks! Season them with cumin roast them on a skillet for a spicy snack. These are popular 'cutters’ or bar foods, made to sober up drunkards. This can be made with chicken gizzards also. Fried chicken livers My mother would carry us to this seedy looking bakery on a Sunday where they served fried chicken livers, mostly to satisfy the patrons of the bar that was situated next to them. You'll spit out its overly pungent flavor at first try but it gets tastier after each bite. Pig tail Pig tail meals are now synonymous with special events such as birthday parties and wedding receptions. Pig tail pelau, as shown above, is made from rice and pig tails cooked in caramelized sugar (stewed) with peas and whatever garnishes desired. There is also pig tail soup. A pig's tail is incredibly meaty, tender and juicy that so much that many people find themselves sucking at the bone upon finishing. Black pudding Thanks to our English rulers of yesteryear who brought this excrement looking sausage, made entirely of pig's blood, to the Caribbean. Our version includes a lot more spices and this dish is quite popular served in bread as a street food. It looks and sounds horrid but it is quite creamy textured and rich in taste. and lastly Cow heel soup Who would've known that a cow's heel would be so gelatinous, meaty and soak up flavour so well. Along with fish broth and corn soup, this is the definitive soup of Trinidad.

Have you ever sabotaged food because someone was stealing it? Is it possible to sabotage someone's lunch by accident? Yes it is. I was the saboteur. The idiot saboteur. Summer was a co-worker of mine at a warehouse I was employed in during my early adulthood. She was a nice girl but she would often get entangled in workplace drama with other provocative and emotional females likes herself. Things got so bad with her that her enemies would go to extreme lengths to sully her reputation or cause harm e.g. calling her boyfriend at night using a private number, spread nasty rumors (some turned out to be true) about her amongst her closest workmates. To work in such an environment could make any girl a little paranoid. Summer was no exception. One faithful afternoon I was about to enjoy my lunch in our staff lunch room. Lunch times were staggered at 12–1pm for some 1–2pm for the rest. I would normally take my lunch at 12pm while Summer took hers afterwards at 1pm. I collected my lunch in the staff fridge and heated it in the microwave. I joined my friends in the 'mess hall’ where we proceeded to have a very exciting conversation about what crap to do with our money when we got paid. While tearing into a chicken drumstick someone made a comment that my mother prepared a really nice lunch for me today. I took a good look down at my lunch bowl and my heart sank. This wasn't my lunch! It was the exact same bowl like mine…..with an orange cover, a little better kept though…..but this was someone else's lunch! I tried to keep my cool. I told my friends I needed to reheat my lunch. Scared to death I would chance upon the true owner coming towards the kitchen, spotting me carrying his/her lunch like a bloody beggar-thief I haphazardly threw the lunch back into the fridge and took out mine. I heated it and returned to my friends like a nervous wreck but eliciting no suspicions. An hour later I'm busy at work when a stern voice comes over the loudspeaker. 'Will all members of staff please report to the kitchen area?’ My heart leaped like stallion in heat. This is it. The s**t has hit the fan. My friends ambled towards me all curious-like saying stuff like 'What the hell is this about?’ and 'Hey, you saw Summer come out from the manager's office in tears? What's her problem now?’ I tried to play it cool but did a terrible job. 'Huh? What da f**k's going on? I got an order to finish. This is bulls**t. Summer is a ho.’ It's a wonder none of them suspected me right then and there. For all staff to be called to a meeting at once meant that this was pretty serious. Somebody's gonna get sent home. My hands started trembling. The warehouse director took center stage and with a wary look on her face explained that Summer had just gone to have her lunch when she observed that it was severely tampered with. She explained that the person tampered with the lunch in such an extreme manner as if to send an insulting, threatening message to her. The director asked that whomsoever did such an act to please reveal him/herself. All the while I stood looking like this: While everyone else around me started to giggle quietly. Summer who stood next to the director stared at me and I immediately looked away. No one came forward. The director gave Summer money to buy lunch. Case dismissed. As we headed back to our respective positions my friends made light banter about the situation. 'We have a food molester at the warehouse. Anyone of us could be the dreaded food molester.’ They then began to laugh. That became a running joke in the warehouse. Twenty minutes later Summer comes towards me and I start to quiver like jelly. 'You see anybody with an orange cover bowl when you were at lunch Elijah?’ I shook my head in the negative. 'Sick f**king people we have working here,’ she continued. 'Yeah.' I said flatly, 'Hmmm.’ 'I mean,’ she continued while raising her voice, 'Interfering with my food? If that person has a problem with me I don't care what they say to my face but to know that some nasty sonofab**ch will go so low…….I mean……. it's just sad…….a sad, sick person.’ 'Yeah.' I replied flatly, 'Boy!……..Hmmm.’ She then stared at me like she did during the meeting. 'Elijah. It was you?’ I feigned a laugh and acted as though it was a joke, 'Yeah. It was me. Who cooked that food girl? Taste real good.’ She smiled and shook her head and went her way. I knew that she suspected the culprit to be a female so I was off the hook. Some years later I am employed elsewhere and I encounter Summer on Facebook. After a brief chat I admitted to her that I was the food molesting culprit. She laughed and said she knew. I asked her how did she know. She said that she found out after the meeting that I had a bowl exactly like hers. She had put 1+1 together. I said, 'So that whole time you spoke to me after the meeting. You knew?’ She said yes. She was playing along with me to judge whether I tampered with her food by accident, as she suspected, or if one of her enemies made me do it……..that my dumb reaction to her comments had said it all. ‘……..It tasted really good though,' was all I could think of saying. Lesson learned: When you tamper with a co-worker's food by accident, it's a good idea to go tell them.

What is the lowest probability event you have personally witnessed? I did a degree in Agribusiness when I attended University. Nutrition and Dietetics students shared the Faculty with us and among the students of N&D was a guy named Gandhi. Gandhi was a short, portly and ambiguously gay chatterbox. He was exceptionally kind and friendly but he loved to have long frivolous conversations that ranged from anything from popular soap operas to university gossip. As an evening student most of my classmates were, oddly enough, middle-aged working women, many of them single mothers and a few of them were grandmothers. Gandhi would come over to our area and chat with us and many of these ladies took an instant liking to him. I, on the other hand, found him a bit too loud, clingy and as mentioned earlier frivolous. One day, my fellow Agribusiness students and I were waiting for a bus. We were to go on a cross country field trip. Gandhi was hanging out with us while we waited and being his usual loud and silly self. One of the students didn't show up so there was room for one on the bus. Gandhi speculated whether the lecturer would allow him to come on the trip even though he wasn't an Agribusiness student. When the bus arrived with the lecturer, Gandhi’s lady friends immediately begged for him to be allowed on the trip. Kind and affable, the lecturer said that since he was in the same faculty he couldn't see it being a problem since there was room for one more. We all boarded the bus. Through chance Gandhi got a seat next to me and from the moment the bus took off and the 6 hrs that followed Gandhi yapped his mouth non-stop. I could not enjoy a single moment of silence to enjoy the sights and sounds with this silly, little man next to me going off on every irrelevant topic that a human could think of during a cross country road trip. To say that my experience was somewhat diminished would be an understatement. Two years after graduating from university my aunt invites me to a trip to Dominica organized by a forestry conservation group. The conservation group was, oddly enough, comprised mostly of middle-aged women and a few grandmothers. On the first day we were to go to a cross country trip on a bus around the little island. Some of the group had opted out of the trip in favour of doing some shopping in the capital Roseau or just relaxing in the hotel. As such I had a seat free to myself next to me. While the bus was driving I was reminded of the cross country trip with Gandhi. The bus driver first took us to the the nearest shops for those who still needed to purchase drinks or snacks. We all went into a little grocery. While browsing the shelves I almost froze when I heard a familiar voice. ‘Elijah?’ it said, ‘What are you doing in Dominica?’ I turned around to see none other than Gandhi himself, like a portly imp-genie who manifests himself whenever one thought about him. Surprised to chance another Trinidadian in the country the group asked me if this was my friend. ‘Uh….’ I said not knowing how to answer that question and feeling a sense of dread, ‘Yeah?’ Gandhi filled them in with the details. I had only just thought about him a few minutes ago and here he was in front of me, in a different country. What were the chances? Here's where it gets even more interesting. Gandhi queried as to what we were doing and they told him of the cross country trip. ‘Oh my God’ I thought. ‘You think maybe I could come?’ Gandhi asked, ‘If it's a matter of money I could pay.’ ‘I don't see why not,’ said our group leader who had taken an instant liking of him. ‘Dont worry,’ she continued, ‘The bus has been already paid for. We have room.’ ‘No f**king way,’ I told myself. Filing back into the bus I hoped to God one of the group members would decide to sit next to me this time. I eyed them all down as they entered, with warm looks, in the vain hope that they change their previous seat and sit to my side, preventing Gandhi from sitting next to me once again. As per fate, that was not to be. Gandhi was the last to enter the bus. He saw my empty seat and immediately sat next to me. I stared at him in a state of wonder and disbelief. I was expecting him to feel the same way. What were the odds of him getting on board a bus that he wasn't meant to be on, with a similar demographic of people, on a similar cross country trip and seated next to the same person on an entirely different country? It was mind-blowing to me. Unfortunately none of this registered in Gandhi's mind. None of this seemed in the least bit strange or fantastic. He simply resumed his barrage of idle banter and irrelevancy for the next four hours.

What's your take on Imane Khelif, a biologically proven male boxer, taking part in the Women's Boxing event at the Paris Olympics 2024? I feel sorry for Imane Khelif. The problem is she premiered in the Olympics at the time when the whole trans women in sports became a hugely divisive and contentious issue, all thanks to this idiot. Inane Khelif has a unique makeup in terms of her gender but was born a female with female genitalia. There was no sex change involved. She is not a man nor a tran. She is just a somewhat masculine woman. Some people don’t realize that she is also someone with feelings. This is the first thing Imane Khelif did after the fight. Look at that photo and tell me you don’t see the face of someone deeply concerned about her opponent. Angela Carini refused to shake Khelif’s hand after her defeat. Carini claimed that Khelif punched harder than anything she felt from any other opponent. She refused to even look Khelif in the face. No one seems to take into regard Khelif is a human being with feelings and that she is now looked upon by the world as some sort of freak before she is even given a chance to speak her story. I am as conservative as they get but in this case I think we are being nothing more than bullies. I have news for people who are angry and want Khelif banished simply because she looks masculine; female boxers/close combat fighters tend to look masculine, in case we’ve forgotten Even Carini has apologized about her post fight comments. Trans women in biological women’s sport is indeed an issue that I’m against but let us not drag Imane Khelif into this ugly fight. She has to take physical blows for a living. It’s not fair that she has to get emotional blows as well.

Which actor played a villain role too well for comfort? Ann Dowd as Joan in Hereditary. ***Spoiler Alert*** The performance by this relatively unknown actress blew me away and everyone who I've known to watch this film. Joan is the motherly figure who befriends Toni Collette's main character Annie who is going through a really tough time. Toni Collette's exemplary performance as a depressed middle aged mother suffering from tragedy is complimented by Ann Dowd's Joan who wins the heart of the viewers as a sympathetic, patient and caring matriarchal figure in the first half, only to suddenly transform into someone truly terrifying in the second half. What was scary for me about her performance was the genuine warmth she generated from the very moment she entered the screen. I can't see anyone being unable to put their guard down and love and accept this lady. It didn't seem like a performance at all. It seemed like that is how Ann Dowd really is. However when she lifts the veil it is almost bloodcurdling to see the transformation in her appearance and especially in her voice. Nothing is more scarier to me than evil people convincingly disguised as good and with that Ann Dowd truly delivered.

What was the "I'm done" moment in your last relationship? I have a 7 year old daughter with my ex. Our relationship was problematic to say the least and for the sake of being allowed to see my daughter I allowed for this 'hanging on a thread’ type relationship to persist for the majority of my daughter's life. My ex (M) and I never communicated well when it came to money. To make a long story short she decided to move out and furnish an apartment of her own whilst I concentrated on getting a house built. My ex had never had her own place and was extremely proud of the fact that she had her own place. To show how proud she was she furnished her apartment with the best television, stereo and appliances that money could buy. For my daughter's birthday I would usually come over with cake, ice cream and the like and we would have a small affair. However two days before my daughter's 6th birthday M calls me and this is the conversation that made me realize that I was done. M: 'I'm having a birthday party for Adrianna.’ Me: 'OK? (pondering why she didn't tell me in advance). Who's coming?’ M: 'My friends from work, my sisters and their children and my mother…..I invited your father too. I am buying the cake and pizza. What are you buying?’ Me: '……..so you told my father about this before you told me?’ M: (Getting noticeably irritated) 'Are you coming or not?’ Me: 'I would've appreciated it if you told me this in advance.’ M: 'So you're saying you don't want to have anything to do with your daughter's birthday?’ Me: 'I never said that.’ M: 'Go f**k yourself.’ She then hangs up the phone. I take some time to compose myself. I was not going to be forced to pay unnecessary money for M's vanity party so she could show off her apartment to her friends and family. In the end I didn't get to see Adrianna on her birthday. I came afterwards to drop my gift and wish her a belated birthday. Instead of expressing remorse over her attitude, M makes inflammatory and untrue comments about how cheap my gift was. I used to tell myself to keep faith and with enough effort M would finally warm over and show more love and respect. However that experience demonstrated that such an ideal would only lead to further pain, disrespect, abuse and her using our daughter as a weapon to get what she wants. The thread finally broke.

What's the biggest anticlimax in movie history? Bird Box (2018) was throughly gripping. All the characters were well fleshed out and relatable and as ridiculous as the premise was (unseen, omnipresent entities that makes one commit suicide if seen) the suspense and horror was so effective it became the most streamed Netflix film at the time, mostly due to word of mouth. SPOILER ALERT But by God what a stupid ending. After so much trauma in the first half of the film, years later Sandra Bullock’s character Malorie and her children (one biological, one adopted) are rowing blindfolded down a dangerous river to find the people who sent her a transmission as to a safe location. After a nail biting odyssey down the river we are all expecting to be given answers when she finally arrives at this mysterious, resistance base. What are those creatures? Where did they come from? What do they want? Why do people kill themselves just by looking at them? What is the state of the world right now? Do the entities have a weakness, is it possible to fight back? Instead the movie does the most dirty tactic that a studio could possible do. Instead of providing the audience what they waited for and dedicated our energy and emotions toward (answers) the studio goes the cheap route and decides to end the film by answering nothing, leaving the film open to sequels and prequels. This is a trend I’ve noticed in a lot of modern horrors and thrillers. They just can't end the effing movie and give us the closure that we waited two hours for. Ranting aside, Malorie reaches the destination, a school for the blind and everyone assures her that everything will be ok in one of the most corniest and cliched endings ever conceived. It’s a pity Malorie didn’t wake up from a dream and see all the familiar faces around her while uttering ‘There’s no place like home.’ I would’ve much appreciated that ending than the actual ending of Bird Box.

What’s your favorite movie based on true events? The Founder (2016) This is a movie I habitually return to watching. It's an inspiring movie but it's not a ‘feelgood’ movie per se. The movie tells the story of how a run of the mill salesman named Ray Kroc outmanoeuvred and outperformed the McDonald brothers and became owner of the McDonald's franchise/empire. I say it's not feelgood because, based on the film, Kroc was not by any account a ‘nice’ man when it came to business. He was a conniving opportunist but at the same time he was also unrelentingly persistent. His partners, the altruistic McDonald brothers derived a brilliant concept and product but had little interest in franchising and/or wealth. It is because of Kroc's persistence and willingness to take great risks that McDonald's is the success that it is today. If there is one concept the movie begs you to take away from it, regardless of your view of Ray Kroc, it is the value of persistence. Without giving away too much of the plot, this is what is inspiring about Kroc's efforts. There are so many profound scenes and quotes in this movie that it find it hard for anyone to not appreciate it for the sole merit that it generates a lot of thought, regardless of whether you don't like it or find Ray Kroc reprehensible. I think Michael Keaton gave his greatest performance and I was thoroughly disappointed that he was not nominated for an Academy Award. His persistence speech at the end of the film, I consider to be a classic in business motivation, trumping that of Jordan Belfort’s ‘sell me this pen’ in The Wolf of Wall Street and Alec Baldwin's ‘Always be closing’ scene in Glengarry Glen Ross. I beg to debate this opinion.

I'm a school custodian and when people ask me what's my job I'm ashamed to tell them. What's the best way I could say what I do without saying I'm a custodian? Embrace the fact that you are a janitor. Yes. I said it. A janitor. You work for a living. You work hard. You are valuable salt of the Earth. People feel comfortable around you and feel more at ease to talk to you because you hold no airs about yourself. People admire you because you do a job that most people don't want and when you do it with pride you are an inspiration. I'm sure if you tell the staff around you your plans to get a degree or invest in a small business you will get an overwhelming amount of support. Everyone loves to see the little guy make small steps. No one likes to hear the big rich CEO gushing about a planned merger or a thriving stock portfolio. No. People love to hear about the janitor who saved his money and started his own cleaning company. You also have the benefit of always knowing who are your real friends. Lawyers, doctors and politicians don't have that benefit. Everyone is running to kiss their ass and use them. Nobody is running to kiss Larry the janitor’s ass and use him. You know that people who don't respect you or your work, no matter how well you perform it, are people to stay away from. You don't have to have your back against the wall to see your enemies. Be proud of who you are. You work hard. Not many people do that. And if anyone asks what you do for a living say with pride that you are a school janitor. Their reaction will say a lot about them Written by a former delivery ‘boy.’

Why do some people not like Coldplay? As probably the only guy answering this question who actually likes Coldplay I’d like to put forward my theory. There are actually two Coldplays. Old Coldplay Modern Coldplay What is the first thing you noticed about the photos? Old Coldplay shows a young band full of awkward post A-Level graduates who don’t care how geeky they look but seem to enjoy each other’s company and being themselves. Modern Coldplay shows an intensely edited photo of four men who are trying their utmost best to look cool and serious. Everything about the photo screams over saturated, highly commercial and bloated. I sincerely doubt the guys even posed together for the photo but rather had separate photos, photoshopped together. Old Coldplay is alternative rock. Yes they wrote a fair share of ballads. Yes they could be whiny, moody and (as another Quora writer has so artfully suggested) ‘sangfroid’ but there was a meticulous attention to instrumentation and songwriting that you can’t listen to songs like Trouble, Clocks and Shiver and call it pop music. They were definitely popular but they weren’t pop. They wrote intelligent songs but with a fair share of technical bravado on their instruments and innovative yet tasteful sound engineering in the same vein of bands like Radiohead and Doves at the time. All old school Coldplay fans would probably share similar sentiments. Us Coldplay fans looked a lot similar to this when we were growing up. Modern Coldplay is an example of commercial pop music at its worst. Take away the sonic instrumental experimentation and instead put in electronic computer programmer loops and samples. Focus more on marketing, publicity and touring rather than on songwriting, innovation and simple band practicing. Throw in a bunch of cringey, force fed collaborations. Envision a basic formula for their craft and then multiply that formula by 300%. (Studio execs: ‘They’re a bit whiny. Let’s make that lead singer go Ohhh ohh ooo every five seconds. That's what the fans seem to like. And let ‘em write a a shitload of slow piano driven ballads. I think they're a woman's rock band. Let them have that guitar player repeating the same derivative chiming hook. In fact toss one of his hooks into the looping software and we'll rework it for an entire album. How about we let each one of them wear a different color? You know like the Spice Girls. Make it seem like they care about stuff around the world like climate change and fair trade and all that crap.’) This is what a modern day Coldplay fan kinda looks like. And that’s why some people don’t like Coldplay. In my humble opinion.

What is the most offensive thing you've been told while out on a date? A decade ago, I went on a date with someone I met on a dating website. I considered myself witty back then and a good few of my jokes had a sarcastic element to them. I met someone on the dating site who seemed to greatly appreciate deadpan quirkiness and sarcasm. She seemed to appreciate it a bit too much than is healthy for the average human. We arranged to meet at the mall. When we saw each other her eyes flitted away from mine and she stared at my shoes. 'That's the shoes you came to see me in?’ She then gave a soft yet caustic 'huh huh huh’ laugh to herself and began what would be a series of rolling eyes at everything that was said. I didn't understand what she meant. The shoes were almost new and were my best pair of sneakers. In fact, compared to her I was overdressed as she wore a rather unflattering suspender-skirt combo and an old pair of sandals. Minus the afro she looked a lot like the photo below but far more unkempt. I decided to ignore the comment. I asked her if she wanted to see a movie and she immediately made this whistling noise and started to go off about mindless dribble that Hollywood dishes out. I sort of agreed with her but at the same time her anti-Hollywood rant came across a bit on the pretentious side. We basically walked around the mall, her making random sarcastic comments about anything in her field of vision and me trying to agree with what she said and keep the conversation flowing. When we parted ways and I went homewards I did a quick mental audit of the date and my conclusion was that she definitely was not my cup of tea. However I told myself that maybe she probably suffers from some sort of anxiety and that's why she behaved so strangely. Maybe I ought to give her a chance. I called to tell her that I enjoyed our time and to find out if she was back home safe. 'Calling to see if I'm home safe?’ she replied, 'Bro. That's so corny. That's like men from the 50s.’ I could hear her faint 'huh huh huh’ laugh and could envision her rolling her eyes. I couldn't help but notice a strong pang of irritation develop within me. I put that aside and we spoke for a bit and ended up agreeing to meet her after she finished her classes the following day (she did a Degree in Computer Science). I told myself that with a little patience she would drop that caustic quirkiness of hers and start showing more warmth . I bought a rose for her and travelled to her school. I told myself what girl wouldn't love a man greeting her outside her class, well dressed and holding a rose for all her peers to see. Being that her class was due to over in a few minutes I basically ran up the street. When I arrived at the school, I called her phone to no avail. I told myself that her class was probably still in session. Then I saw a bunch of students filing out and I knew that she had to be among them. I saw her at the back, looking particular slovenly staring at me with her usual vacant stare. 'Oh my God.’ I saw her mouth the words as I moved towards her with the rose. However she mouthed it in distaste as though I were brandishing a slimy toad. As I reached within earshot she said the single most offensive thing I've ever heard someone mutter to me during a date. 'I was hoping you didn't come.’ This was followed by her 'huh huh huh’ laugh and rolling eyes. The irritation from the day before changed to anger. I tried to put aside the statement as another of her offbeat quirkiness and told her passionately about my hasty journey to get to her and how I ran up the street so as not to have her waiting. 'Dude,' she replied, 'That's psycho talk. Shut up.’ I paused and looked at her for a long while. Her supposed sense of humour was truly starting to rub me the wrong way. It sounded like a joke but came across like a vent fashioned into a rude and unfunny joke. She then talked about how she saw phone calls but intentionally disregarded them in the hopes that I would go away. She then mentioned that she saw me running up the street like a madman with a rose in my hand and felt so embarrassed. I remained silent. It was now a code red. Either I give her a piece of my mind or bow gracefully and leave. I opted for the latter and waited for a good civil moment to depart. 'You look like the type who doesn't go anywhere,' she continued, 'Seeing how you just ran through the streets just to see me from class you probably don't go out much. My ex boyfriend was a DJ. I used to get in to all the parties for free. He wasnt much to look at but a little sex now and again and I got into all the exclusive parties…..even aboard yachts. You know what a yacht is right?’ I remained silent. 'Dunno why I'm telling you all this………Look at you.You look like you want knock my head off don't you. Huh huh huh.’ It then dawned upon me that this girl was a twisted individual. This wasnt some quirky sense of humour. This was someone who got their kicks off of provoking others. Whatever hurt she experienced from those she loved in the past, she clearly wanted to exact that hurt on innocent people around her. When she arrived at her taxi stand I stood and waited in silence until she got into one. 'Well look at you,' she said in a last desperate attempt for a reaction from me, 'My knight in shining armour... You should maybe think about buying a car……it's kinda lame that…' The taxi driver sped off without waiting for her to finish what she was saying, probably cognizant that she was someone full of shit. I went home proud of myself that I didn't give her the reaction she desired. I deleted my account on the dating site. After that encounter I became far more conservative towards the use of sarcasm in humour and communication. I've been attracting much more likable and attractive females ever since that minor adjustment. So everything truly is a learning experience.

What things do people say that make you roll your eyes? A guy from my neighbourhood came to my house some time ago asking for help. He had gotten a flat tire and wanted to borrow my spare for the following day as he needed to check out a job in the morning. From the moment we started speaking to the moment we parted, our conversation was a series of eye rolling on my part. Me: So how come you don't have a spare? Him: I just bought an amp and some speakers. Money’s finished. My car probably has the best music setup in the whole street. Me: (At his house) But look you have another car here. Why don't you use this car? Him: That car isn't working. Me: Then why don't you use one of the tires. It's the same size. Him: That's not my car that's my wife's. Wife (comes out to say hello, seemingly drunk): I have a car for sale. If you only see the engine on this car. Proceeds to open the hood on the car previously mentioned. Me: But is this car working? Wife: Who says it's not working? (glares at husband). Me: (Looking at the engine) Why are there sunflower seeds on top the carburetor? Wife: That damn parrot! It acts as if this car is his house. Husband: I'm actually a mechanic myself. Me: (Tempted to say ‘But you can't fix your wife's car?’) Mmhmm. Husband: I have practically every tool there are for cars. Me: (Tempted to say ‘But you don't have a spare tire.’) Mmhmm Husband: If ever you need work done on your car be sure to check me. Me: Will do. Husband: Can I borrow your tire wrench? I can't find mine. Husband: I can do masonry, plumbing, electrical, roofing. Wife: He's very talented. I never have to call anybody to get work done. I have an entire contracting company living in my house. Husband: Take my number. (He proceeds to search for a call card in his wallet but the area is in darkness.) Honey shine a light on my wallet for a second. Me: Why don't you put up some lights in the front yard? Husband: (Says nothing) Wife: (Scowling) The man just asked you a question. Husband: Well your spare didn't fit but thanks for the help anyway. Me: No problem. Husband: Can you do me one more favour? Me: (groaning) What? Husband: (Whispering so his wife, who went back in the house, doesn't hear). Can you lend me $20? I’ll need it for gas in the morning. Me: Sure (hands him a $20) Husband: (whispering even softer) You want a beer? Me: Yeah why not. Husband: If I go with you she'll know that I'm going for alcohol. You don't mind going to the grocery and getting it for us. (Hands me back my $20) Me: (Puts $20 back in wallet). Sure thing man. I then went home. I wonder how long he waited until it dawned on him that I was not coming back with his beers.

What are some examples of style without substance in writers? I know I may be critized for some of my choices but these are some of the works I've read that I deeply consider to be style heavy but severely lacking in substance imho. Fight Club — Chuck Palahniuk The cult status of this novel has become almost legendary after the film debut in 1999. Back then I thoroughly enjoyed the film for its defiantly anarchist undertones and its twist ending. As I've grown older the film now seems a tad ridiculous and childish and the so-called twist ending makes absolutely no sense in retrospect. Our of curiosity I read the book and it further confirmed my sentiments that the book/movie was written solely for an audience of angst-ridden males between the ages of 16 — 25. Palahniuk's style is some sort of mish-mash stream of consciousness dialogue combined with frenetic pacing, little concern for character development, cliffhangers around every corner and throws in a random fact few pages (gasoline and orange juice can be used to make napalm……oooh {angst filled teen wets himself}. The Beach — Alex Garland Another 90s, stream of consciousness, style heavy writer who's found enormous success with the titular novel which found its way to the big screen back in 2000. Like Fight Club this novel was aimed at disenchanted 16 — 25 year olds tired of the rat race, capitalism etc. More meaningless pretentious philosophizing, even less character development, throw in a dash of romance, a pinch of melodrama, a teaspoon of surrealism and you have a style heavy book that (just like Fight Club) leans on a great idea rather than on good writing. The Short-Timers — Gustav Hasford Another style heavy novel that coulda been. This Vietnam war account is the basis for the famous film Full Metal Jacket (1987) by Stanley Kubrick. Kudos to Kubrick who did away with Hasford's overbearing stoner prose and stuck to the meat of the novel which was the clever boot camp dialogue and harrowing recruit training. The book is semi autobiographical. It seems as though the moment Hasford is free to roam the streets of Vietnam his writing became almost unreadable in a drug induced haze of (again) stream of consciousness babble. Black Spring — Henry Miller One may be surprised to find an established writer like the controversial Henry Miller on this list but after turning the obscene into an art form with Tropic of Cancer he wrote Black Spring which becomes rather unreadable and unintelligible after the first few pages. Miller's gift is to seize your attention within the first few lines in his writing. He shocks you with his unwholesome combination of literary mastery combined with smut and depravity. He explodes within the first few pages with prose so electric that even George Orwell dedicated an essay in praise of him. However his flaw is his inability to sustain this style at length as he goes from captivating to dull and rambling. Black Spring is a perfect example of that flaw. And last but not least The Trial — Franz Kafka Yes. One of the world's greatest writers is also guilty of style over substance, most noticeably in the above stated novel. If there is one author who has cemented a style for himself it has to be Kafka as kafkaesque is now an accepted English word for anything related to paranoia and fantastic surrealism inspired through stifling bureaucracy. The Trial is not a bad book imho. In fact it is the most representative of his style. However one cannot help but lean towards believing whether the work is a testament to his genius or the whimsical ramblings of lonely, neurotic mild-mannered man. I tend to lean towards the latter as halfway through the novel it seems as though his unique style can't help but disguise the fact that there is no real story of substance happening. But these are all my honest opinions. Love em or hate em.

What is one thing that all men hate? Yesterday I was at home. I couldn't attend work because my area had been flooded for the third time in a month. It was both nerve-wracking and boring being stuck in a house surrounded by water and fearful that the rain falls and the water gets higher and enters inside. I get a missed call. It's from a lady at work who is notorious for always wanting something. Practically every encounter I've had with her usually ends up with her saying 'I wanted to ask you about…… ’ Or 'Would it be alright if I…..’ Or 'Next Monday I wanted to……' In other words she wanted a favour from me. This is all fine and dandy but truly I only like to perform favours to people I consider friends. By no stretch of the imagination do I consider her a friend and the sheer volume of favours she's asked me over the years is exponentially greater than the favours every friend of mine has ever asked me combined. I decided to not take the call. Moments later I see that she sends a voice message. I call my girlfriend and discuss whether I should ignore it and she tells me. 'What if the lady just wants to know if you're alright?’ I then feel guilty. Maybe I am being a bit cynical. I decide to listen to the voice message. I play it; 'Hi. Didn't see you in work today. Hope everything is ok….’ In my mind I said my girlfriend was right and I shouldn't be so presumptuous. However, I then hear a sentence that makes me recoil. 'Since you're not here I was wondering if I could use your office to….’ I stopped listening. I didn't reply. I think every single man would agree that we hate when people only seek after us to get favours done.

What's the most obnoxious instance of America-centric behavior you've ever witnessed? During my first week at Papa John’s (Trinidad) the phone rang and I took the call. An American accent could be heard on the other end of the line. Caller: I’ll have the Friday special Me: Sorry ma’am but the specials are from Sundays - Wednesdays. Caller: This is Papa John’s right? Me: Yes. Caller: Papa John’s has Friday specials where I’m from. What’s the special for today? Me: Sorry but the specials are only from Sundays - Wednesdays. Caller: I’m goin’ write a review about the Papa John’s in Trinidad. I’ve traveled the world. I’ve never encountered any Papa John’s that doesn’t have a daily special. I want to talk to the manager. I call Ricardo, the manager, and he takes the phone. I’m expecting him to repeat what I said but instead he says ‘yes’ every few seconds and on the screen I see him enter two extra large pizzas, a large garlic bread sticks, a large cheese bread sticks and a 2L soda. He’s entering all these items, not as any discounted ‘special,’ but at retail value, so the bill is fairly sizable. He then covers the receiving end of the phone with his palm and tells me, ‘Go check and see if there’s any brownies left. I went in the chiller and saw two brownies remaining. I showed him two fingers and watch as he enters them both on the lady’s bill. He repeats the order to the caller. ‘So the total will be $502………no miss that is in Trinidad dollars. Yes miss that is a good deal you are getting…….OK…….Yes we take Mastercard………20 minutes…………thank you.’ He hung up the phone and looked at me smiling. ‘How did you manage to sell her all that stuff?’ I said, ‘She wanted a special.’ ‘I did give her a special,’ he says with a mischievous smile, ‘Ricardo’s special.’ He then proceeds to laugh flamboyantly and heads back to his office while saying, ‘Whenever you hear an American accent on the phone just call me…….I have a $10,000 sales target to make today.’

Which supporting actress was much more memorable than the star of a movie? Toni Collette gave one of the greatest performances ever rendered on film in the soon to be cult classic Hereditary (2018) but another actress outshined her by a fraction of a fraction. Ann Dowd gave a most chillingly deceptive performance of Joan, a warm and empathetic older lady who befriends Collette's character Annie as she struggles with tragedy, resentment and depression. The beauty of Ann's performance is her complex nuances. She transforms from a lovable, nurturing Aunt May type character that was so understated yet genuinely compassionate to a different being one would've never predicted her to be near the ending. The most common description I've heard about her character for those who've enjoyed the film is how 'real’ Joan seemed. Ann Dowd is one of the most underrated actresses of the 21st century. No one can play matriarchal type figures like her and even the most hardened scoundrel would find themselves letting down their guards and engaging a sense of love and trust in the warmth she emanates. Therefore it's startling when that different side of her comes out during the final 20 minutes of the film. I'm not giving spoilers because YOU NEED TO GO SEE HEREDITARY IF YOU HAVENT SEEN IT YET.

Can you provide some examples of average actors delivering great performances due to well-written characters? Let's be frank. Samuel L. Jackson is a one trick pony. But gosh darn it that sure is one hell of a trick that motherf****n pony does. All jokes aside I find it hard to think of Quintin Tarantino writing the character Jules without envisioning Samuel L. Jackson in mind for the role in Pulp Fiction. It is truly the role Jackson was born to play. It is the role that took Jackson into stardom and to this day Jules’ intimidating obscenity ridden threats, interrogation, debates on burgers and pork, not to mention his love of quoting Ezekiel 25:17 is constantly memed, quoted and parodied. But I wouldn't consider Jackson a great actor. He may sit more comfortable with his tough guy roles but he isn't anywhere near the range of other legendary tough guy actors like Denzel Washington, Clint Eastwood and James Cagney. If you know Jackson is going to be in a movie you are certain that he isn't going to be a bespectacled data programmer hunched behind a computer or a main love interest. He is probably the most famous typecast of Hollywood film history since John Wayne. It's a bit unfortunate because when he attempts more vulnerable or intellectual characters it comes across as forgettable at best and eerie at worst in my honest opinion (Tarzan, RoboCop, Star Wars). I don't think Sam may get another role as defining and well written as Jules in Pulp Fiction. I think a large portion of his filmography isn't impressive from an acting standpoint. He may not be a Marlon Brando or a Laurence Olivier but neither of them could've put in the heart and energy into an intricately moulded character such as Jules Winnfield.

What guitarists do you think have the most emotionally moving solos? I love this question because it's entirely subjective and for someone who has zero technical guitar knowledge and even less skills, I can answer it. It's rare that I sense a feeling of emotion in a guitar solo. Most solos to me just sound like cool improvisations that take you away from the rigidity of the melody and repetition of verse-chorus, verse-chorus. There are only a handful of songs that I've actually felt the emotion behind the playing. It's like the guitarist is talking to you with his guitar and you sense the emotions behind the words. Such are the best examples I can think of: Carlos Santana — Samba Pa Ti. This is possible the best example I can think of in regards to emotional solos. The entire song is basically an extended guitar solo. Wrought with the feelings of longing, regret and desire this song is one of the artist's most impressive contribution. I can hear a man at his wit's end wailing to lost love from the very first few notes. Buck Dharma — Don't Fear The Reaper Nothing is more terrifying than the ominous solo in this pre-heavy metal classic. I get visions of demonic creatures rising from beneath when this manic, blistering guitar starts going off after a creepy rhythm guitar intro. Buck Dharma wrote the song after envisioning death for himself and it shows in his playing. Jimi Hendrix — Little Wing Funny how this original composition grew from obscurity to one of his most covered songs. 'Fly on, Little Wing' Hendrix indeed takes us to soaring heights with this solo full of wonder, hope and optimism. I consider the solo an extension of the themes explored in another Hendrix classic The Wind Cries Mary. Play both solos one after the the other and you'll see what I mean. John Frusciante — Scar Tissue In the land of weeping guitars Scar Tissue reigns King. The greatest achievement of the Red Hot Chili Peppers in regards to their sombre, non funky output. Frusciante's guitar sounds like a broken down and dying animal. Figures that it is shown to be literally broken in the music video. Jonny Greenwood — Paranoid Android + There There Couldn't choose between the two Radiohead classics but they both explore the emotions of fear, paranoia and anxiety. Paranoid Android's solo is fractured yet blistering. It is cold and unconventional yet wrought with feelings, like an android having a physical and emotional breakdown. There There’s rhythm and solo combined instills a deeply fearful feeling of slowly incurring the wrath of some powerful unseen entity. And lastly Duane Allman — Melissa The slide guitar to end all slide guitar. A grandeur solo like no other is encapsulates themes of freedom, love and innocence. Duane's guitar makes its presence from the very beginning and soars to the heavens in its solo. Given the fact that Duane Allman died not long after creating this marvellous piece of work does one sense an almost spiritual connection with Duane's playing on this a masterpiece.

What is the creepiest thing that happened to you and you never forgot? (image altered for legal reasons) For a few hours, a grown ass man like myself experienced exactly how a female feels to be manipulated by someone you place your trust and sexually harassed. I was 22 and out of a job. I became so desperate I went to my old Secondary (High) School to ask for a job recommendation letter from a teacher. Unfortunately I arrived at the school too late as most of the teachers had left. There was this large, hulking man with a shiny bald head, dressed professionally and with a calm, collective manner about himself. I never saw him before. He introduced himself to me as Mr. O.J, a new substitute teacher. He was somewhere around 6 feet tall, looked well over 200 pounds of muscle and could be somewhere in his late 20’s to mid 30’s. I took a shot in the dark and asked him if he could write a recommendation for me. He diplomatically replied that it would be dishonest of him seeing that I was never his student. I respected his honesty and was about to bid him adieu when he stopped me and asked if I was interested in becoming a teacher. ‘Yeah,’ I replied. I told him how I tried to apply with the Ministry of Education but they kept turning me away. He then explained to me that he knows a secret method to get into the teaching service. That this method got him his job the day after he applied. I asked if this ‘secret’ was basically him having some connection with some big shot in the Ministry of Education. He said no. He explained that it was much more complicated and that he couldn’t discuss it here because he could get himself into trouble. I inquired as to whether he was going to use this method to get me into the service. He replied that he would help me. He said to leave my number and he will make the necessary calls and arrangements and he would get back to me when I’m successful. I gave him my number, thanked him and left. As I exited the compound I thought it was kind of strange that he found it dishonest to write a simple letter of recommendation, yet he would take a leap of faith and expose his ‘secret’ to secure me a job as a teacher. I simply told myself that he was just a nice, helpful guy. That very evening I got a call from him. There was a rather playful tone in his voice, much different to his professional manner earlier. He explained to me that I was in luck, his acquaintance in the Ministry said that there were positions for substitute teachers and if I wanted I could get a post in my old school. That was great news. I loved my old Secondary school and was missing it very much since I graduated 3 years earlier. He asked if I was interested. I told him very much so. He told me he would have to meet me somewhere so that I can sign the application form. I agreed to meet him Saturday. I was an Evening student at the University of the West Indies (UWI) and so was he, so we agreed to meet there as we both had classes that day. After the arrangement was confirmed I was hoping to end the call on a brisk, business-like note. Mr. O.J. however, became rather frivolous and began to ask me questions about my life while upkeeping silly, irrelevant banter. He kept referring to how I ‘looked like a player’ and that I probably had a bunch of girlfriends while I attended school. I felt awkward and slightly uncomfortable talking girly talk with a large, grown ass bald headed man. Thankfully this lasted but a few minutes as he took the hint that I didn’t like the direction of the conversation. He reminded me of the arrangement on Saturday and wished me a good night. I told myself he was probably lonely and lacking in the friends department. That could make anybody socially awkward. Despite the weirdness, everything seemed legit. I had not the slightest suspicion of any agenda. We were meeting in a crowded area at a respected institution. I knew his name and his place of work, so clearly any scheme from him could only put himself at risk career-wise. Or so I thought. We met at the University on a sunny Saturday morning. I was dressed casually in a pair of cargo shorts and a T-shirt. Mr. O.J. came eerily dressed in office wear even though it was the weekend and he was off duty. I was expecting him to come with a folder full of documents to sign but all he carried on him was a beaten up, old Netbook. I wished him good morning and he stared me deep in the eyes and smiled, replying good morning softly. It was then I realized that he had a habit of unflinchingly staring at me. I waited for him to explain what the hell was supposed to happen from here when he mentioned that he was hungry to the point of starving. He hinted whether I could see about getting the food while he find a spot where he could get a good WiFi signal. I thought this was a rather thoughtless and inconsiderate thing to suggest: I was unemployed with little funds to go about, he had a salary and was asking me to get him food. I couldn’t protest because I needed his help to get this job. The cheapest thing that I could get was some doubles (fried bread with chickpeas). I bought him two but couldn’t afford any for myself. I found him at some benches outside the gymnasium. Due to it being the weekend, the population was but a handful of students. I sat opposite Mr. O.J. and watched in disgust as he scoffed down the two doubles like a vacuum cleaner. It was unbecoming of the professional character he took pains to establish. It seemed that he wasn’t lying when he said he was starving. There was a trickle of sauce at the corner of his lips when he was ready to begin the formal, job application procedure. I told him to wipe his face and then he beckoned me to sit next to him. He then flipped open the battered netbook and for ten painstaking minutes he attempted to get a decent WiFi signal. During these arduous ten minutes he peppered me with more prying and out of place conversation. He described his house that he was building and how his lecturer told him his thesis could probably earn him a scholarship. He kept chuckling to himself and would croon old R&B songs out loud. A group of good looking girls passed and stared at us oddly. I felt deeply embarrassed. I told myself he’s either gay or mad or both. I had no problem with gay guys but I think that every gender and sexual orientation is obligated to respect the boundaries of others regardless of the norms of their intimate circle. Mr. O.J. clearly didn’t believe in boundaries as he continued to pester me personal questions and behave inappropriately. When the WiFi finally kicked in, I breathed a sigh of relief. I had had enough of him and his attempts at being ‘close’ to me. I wanted to sign whatever document there was to sign and leave.
