What screams "I make terrible financial decisions!"? I worked with a lady in her early 40s at a pizza restaurant. She was just a ordinary grunt like the rest of us. She aspired to be a supervisor but what held her back was that she had 6 kids, three, in their late teens/early adulthood for one father, another two of toddler age for another father and a baby for her recent boyfriend. This domestic situation made it hard for her punctuality and regularity at work as there was always a babysitting issue or child maintenance issue that needed resolving with her two exes. Her current boyfriend was no supportive stalwart himself as practically once every week she would stop her duties to go outside the restaurant to have long and intense arguments with him on the phone in regards to his inability to come pick her up that evening or various other disagreements that they had. In person the boyfriend had a nasty, arrogant attitude and seemed to care only for casual sex, his car and for her to keep his baby away from her older kids whom they all shared a mutual dislike with one another. She lived with her two toddlers and her baby at her father's house which was shared with several other siblings of similar circumstance. With that there was a lot of family fighting in regards to space and ownership. To put it bluntly she lived in a world of shit. Given the circumstances it seemed unlikely that she would be unable break free from the poverty and drudgery any time soon. I would feel the greatest sympathy for her and try my best to help her at work in any regards. That is until that fateful day when I saw her rubbing her stomach and smiling to herself. ‘Looks like you're ready for another one (baby)’ I said jokingly. She smiled and said that she and her current boyfriend (the arrogant dickhead) was trying for another baby. They had a girl and now he wanted a boy. ‘Are you serious?’ I said. I was flabbergasted that she was saying this so casually. It was as if she suddenly reverted back to a naive 16 yr old who found her first love and was no longer a middle aged woman with 6 children and a truckload of problems. One of my biggest flaws is that sometimes I can't keep my opinions to myself. ‘But you have 6 kids already!’ For a second she came out of her dream and reverted back to reality. She glared at me angrily for a split second .Then she returned to her child like persona and replied, ‘Children are a blessing.’ ‘Children are a blessing when you can afford to raise them right and give them the love and attention they need.’ Those words just came out of me in very emphatic tone. As a father of one (I worked part time at the restaurant) I was struggling to survive, working two jobs to ensure that my daughter had a future and to ensure all of my free time was dedicated to her. This lady worked one job and was dependent on family, friends and the Government to assist with any shortcomings she encountered, which seemed to be every day. I could not relate at all to what she was saying. She glared at me again and the conversation ended. An hour later I'm called into the manager's office. Apparently she got so angry she complained to the manager that I was being emotionally abusive, chauvinistic (the restaurant was 90% female staff) and stuck my nose in other people's business. She even told the manager that my words were so hurtful she felt overcome with hurt that she was considering taking a sick day and leaving. I sat and nodded in silence. I was the given a warning and sent out of the office. I learned a sad but valuable lesson that day: Some people are simply destined for a life of hardship and misery through their own stubborn mentality and poor choices. So to answer the question What screams "I make terrible financial decisions!"?: People who get offended by the truth.

Can you name an actor who was never a good actor but became one? Sterling Hayden never wanted to be an actor. He was coaxed into the profession as a young, handsome sailor whose photogenic good looks appealed to a post WWII audience who were just begging for actors who were the image of tall and rugged manliness. The 6′5 blonde, athletic young shipmate got into the industry after a 1938 photo gained popularity in a fisherman's magazine. Dubbed by Paramount as 'The Beautiful Blond Viking God’ he got into the industry as a means to purchase his own ship but grew to resent Hollywood. His early roles were a slew of rather forgettable Westerns and film noirs. After his role in the classic Western Johnny Guitar starring Joan Crawford he became a bonafide star. However around this time his personal life got more attention as he was reported to have communist sympathies during the McCarthy/Red Scare era and during a vicious custody battle for his children he took his four children on a self manned trip aboard his ship Wanderer from San Francisco Bay to Tahiti despite the legal implications that awaited him at home. His impulsive nature, hatred of Hollywood,anti- capitalism sentiments and sometimes reckless behaviour gave him the image of an eccentric, of which is well documented in his autobiography Wanderer (1963). However upon working with Stanley Kubrick in The Killing he found his niche playing manic and impulsive characters, not far removed from his actual personality. His best role arguably being that of the insane American General Jack D. Ripper in Kubrick's classic black political comedy Dr. Strangelove. His final great role was that of corrupt Irish police Captain Mark McCluskey in The Godfather (1972). Despite the critical and commercial resurgence his roles and his writings were used solely to fund his travels of which (along with legal expenses and taxes) he continuously saw his money decrease. He died of prostate cancer at the of 70 in 1986, leaving behind six children.

What television shows started strong only to become unwatchable later? Skins (2007 - 2013) The show was highly popular with millennials as it strove to give a realistic depiction of teenaged adults of that generation. The show, with its graphic portrayal of promiscuous sex and drug use among the majority of its main cast made it controversial at the time. Themes such as anorexia, poverty, depression, trauma, dysfunctional parenting etc were also touched on without succumbing to preaching or caricature. In essence the show was a comedy that subtly touched on some of the drama that went on in the personal lives of each of its characters. Generation 1 Without a doubt the first generation of Skins (Series 1 -2) is the true representation of the show. The first two seasons chronicles the lives of the above 9 teenagers. I enjoyed how no one was treated as the star of the show. Everyone had their positive traits as well as deep seated flaws but no one is given more screen time over the other or made into a token. The show focused on the youths as a group rather than as an hierarchy. The lifestyle may have been a tad exaggerated in its insistence that every character supposedly engaged in promiscuous sex and/or drug use. Besides that the show was an honest representation of teenaged millennials, written by an actual millennial, Jamie Brittain, who was 22 at the premier of the first season. The show launched the careers of actors Nicholas Hoult and Dev Patel who portrayed Tony and Anwar respectively. Generation 2 The second generation of Skins (Series 3–4) saw some changes. The comedic tone was increased as well as the amount of sex. The third season started off with an air of superficiality compared to the first generation but had a few well written moments and thoughtful episodes, particularly that of the trials and tribulations of teenaged Congolese immigrant Thomas. However the cast seemed all over the place and without developed characterization except that of cheap stereotypes (bully, geek, skater boy, drama queen, femme fatale etc.) Unlike Generation 1, this generation seemed to have an hierarchy among the cast as everything seemed to revolve around the characters Effy and Cook, who were, unsurprisingly, the most promiscuous and morally unscrupulous of the lot. Nearing the end of series 3 the show's writing started to wear thin. Shocks, drama and comedy were shoehorned in at every chance available. The show and its characters started losing their sense of direction and some of the themes that made them compelling characters in the beginning were abandoned in favour of sex and silliness. Some episodes were so ludicrous it became an effort to keep my eyes on the screen. The show seemed like a poor man’s imitation of itself. (So he's stealing a boat now…?) By series 4 it became painful to watch and I gave up. I have no intention to watch the third generation nor the American MTV remake. However the first generation of Skins remains a classic in my mind and a damned brilliant character study. It's hard for any writer to keep such a momentum going so you got to give the creators of the show credit for trying, even if they tried too hard in the end.

What show / movie had no right to be as good as it was? Back in 1999 my brother and I was spending some summer vacation time at our cousin's place in Tobago. It wasn't the greatest of vacations because our cousin and her boyfriend were having these vicious fights over money (they weren't in the best place financially and had four daughters below the age of 5). We decided to spend a Saturday afternoon going to the cinema. We didn't care what was on, we just wanted to get away from the endless arguments amidst the chaos of screaming toddlers and mounds of filthy diapers. This was the double feature of the weekend: As a pair of hormone raging, ignorant and slightly sexist teenage boys, you could guess which movie appealed to us more. We were grateful that the 007 movie was showing first so we wouldn't have to stick around to watch Double Jeopardy or as my brother called it The Fugitive….but with a Woman. When The World Was Not Enough ended with its typical 007 sexual innuendo type final scene my brother and I looked at each other and nodded. It was ok. There was a lot of explosions, chase scenes, Denise Richards’ bouncing breasts and shorty shorts but we both knew we were unimpressed. However, in our typical peer influenced macho-vision we pretended that the movie was the real deal. We had the choice of watching Ashley Judd outrun a police car or go home and face adults yelling while half naked toddlers pee themselves in fright. We decided to watch the movie. What a great decisions that was. Double Jeopardy was like a roller coaster ride that got better by the minute. It was far better than The World is Not Enough. It was even better than The Fugitive. When she got her poetic justice in the end my brother and I jumped from our seats and wanted to hug each other in tears. We could give a fart about our macho ideals, Ashley Judd was our sister and she finally been done right. It was that good of a movie! We left the cinema thoroughly satisfied and entertained in so much that the choas that awaited us home didn't seem to matter anymore. I recently rewatched it with the idea that maybe it wasn't that great and maybe because we were dumb teenagers it had made an impression. I was blown away even moreso a thirty something year old dad than as a thirteen year old boy. The movie abandons every cliche there is about on-the-run and fugitive type action thrillers. The lead role is no superhero, there is no stupid forced comic relief character making racist jokes, there is no romantic subplot. Straight up escape and revenge served on a hot plate with Tommy Lee Jones in his best performance ever imho. I sincerely recommend it.

Which character did you view totally differently as a child vs. as an adult? Roy Neary - Close Encounters of the Third Kind If there is one character who deserves the award for biggest douchebag protagonist Richard Dreyfuss’ performance of Roy Neary wins that award by a wide margin. He's a blue collar, salt of the Earth electrician, an honest man with a loving wife and two kids. While driving home at night he has an encounter with UFOs and his life suddenly changes dramatically. Without giving away too much of the story I'll concentrate on his character. As a child I saw Roy Neary as a hero, a distressed and eccentric one but a hero nonetheless. He worked relentlessly to uncover a secret Government rendezvous between humans and aliens about to happen in his area. He overcame all obstacles set forward by the Government, the army, secret service and his own family leaving him to prove himself right; that aliens and UFOs did indeed exist and the Government was indeed staging a landmark meeting between man and intelligent extraterrestrial life forms. Roy takes it even a step further. In the final moments of the movie he offers himself to the aliens and boards their ship amidst dozens of alien children. We are then treated to a rousing score accompanied by the beautiful flashing lights of the mothership as it majestically floats off into the sky and the credits roll. It is a fantastic scene full of wonder and innocence that only the likes of Spielberg could deliver. The End That is how I saw the film as a child. As an adult it was a completely different experience. Roy Neary was this a-hole who could give two farts about his wife and kids and all his responsibilities in life. His family didn’t leave him because they were impatient with his alien obsession, in fact they were remarkably patient with his bullshit. He stopped working and stopped caring about anything that didn’t involve anything regarding secret Government cover ups and aliens. However when he begins thrashing the house to build a model Devil’s Tower mountain and becoming a threat to himself, his family and neighbours are they forced to evacuate the premises in a state of trauma. Some people theorize that Roy was under some sort of mind control by the aliens and his actions were not willfully done, that everything was planned and coordinated by the alien masterminds. I argue that Roy was just a big A-hole. Why would the aliens have Roy come close to sabotaging the secret meeting with his annoying shenanigans? Roy acts with little intelligence and self control throughout most of the movie. He's like a selfish, impetulant and irresponsible child that must be the first in line to get the latest Playstation in stores. He has an ‘Us and them’ mentality whereby if you weren't an actual UFO witness or some half-cracked alien conspiracy theorist he didn't care about what you said and law and order didn't exist. I think Roy is a big stain on a great movie. When you think about it, none of his actions benefited anyone. Jillian would've gotten back her son regardless if she went Devil's Tower or not and his discovery would amount to nothing because no one would believe him afterwards. He ruined his family all so he could see some cool alien stuff and weasel his way into the heart of a grieving single mom. His character is supposed to be redeemed by offering himself to the aliens. To me he is just this UFO geek that wanted to escape paying child support. Lacombe: Monsieur Neary. You can't go aboard zat space sheep. What about your madame and infants? Neary:……my work here is done.

What’s your relationship with alcohol? As a self-described connoisseur of fine liquor I have to honestly say that my relationship with alcohol has reached something of a close. In my mid to late 20s, when I started to drink habitually, one stiff drink used to give me a solid buzz/near drunkenness that lasted a couple hours. A 750ml bottle of rum, vodka, whisky or scotch with a chaser of choice could last me a month and change. However this frugality was because I had little alcohol tolerance and was prone to hangovers. Excessive drinking was not greatly desired unless I had friends over or something to celebrate. In my early to mid 30s, what I consider my peak age of drinking, two stiff drinks gave me a solid buzz and anything over that got me into the tipsy/drunken spectrum. This lasted about two hours at most and I had great tolerance. Hangovers ceased to exist for me, partially due to experience but mostly due to self discipline. However my urge to drink started growing and I started to feel come downs more strongly and frequently. Now I’m in my late 30s. It takes me three stiff drinks to get a solid buzz that lasts 30 minutes to an hour. After this my come down lasts practically the rest of the evening and lingers into the next day. The urges are so strong that sometimes the first place I'm drawn to in a grocery is the liquor section. A 750ml bottle wouldn't last me more than a week at the height of my urges. The funny thing about alcohol is that when I reach that peak whereby my buzz is at its strongest but I've not yet condescended into drunkenness, I feel as though I’ve manifested into my supreme self. It tricks me into thinking my mind operates deeper and much more efficiently under its influence. The day I found on my phone a ‘supreme self’ video recording I did of me slurring and rambling about deep, self discoveries through alcohol, it did me a favour and proved otherwise. I'm not a shitty person when I'm drunk. Nobody has a problem with me intoxicated. I've never become uncouth, aggressive or self destructive when I drink. I'm a shitty person during the come down. I become sullen, withdrawn and easily irritated. I lose sight of my goals and ambition and I tend to focus on all my disappointments in life which opens the floodgate to anxiety and depression. I've come to the stage where alcohol takes away a lot more than it gives. Yeah, the occasional beer or cocktail makes me feel relaxed, temporarily kicks out my fears and anxieties and can even give me a boost of confidence but now I’ve found myself at an odd stage in my life where my body is both desirous of alcohol and yet repelled by it. As such I've been weaning off of harder liquor and instead been having an occasional drink of my own homemade fruit wines when the urges come. My wines are admittedly less than stellar and with an alcohol percentage so low it makes Coors Light look like absinthe. However even though weaning from alcohol has stopped me from feeling like Alexander the Great for an hour or so, it sure beats feeling like Eeyore the Donkey for hours on end afterwards.

What are the best and the worst movie posters ever? The Best You know how as a child practically anything could impress you. You see Bio-Dome (1996) as a 10 year old and Pauly Shore is the greatest comedian to walk the face of the Earth. Or, nothing is as terrifying as this scene in Ernest Scared Stupid (1991) And of course, no science-fiction could match the imaginative, voyeuristic spectacle of Jane Fonda in Barbarella (1968). But then you grow older and revisit these movies to feel that same sense of awe as a child only to ask yourself 'Did I really like this s**t!?’ It happens to me all the time. One movie that didn't disappoint when returning to it was Terminator 2: Judgement Day (1991). I managed to get to see it in cinema as a 5 year old with my family and I can't forget the moment I glanced upon that iconic poster of Arnie clad in leather jeans and jacket, straddling a Harley Davidson while clutching a shotgun with one eye glowing red amidst a cold, steely blue background. Let's look at it again. It sent exciting shivers down my spine as a toddler and it still manages to have the same effect as a grown ass man. The Worst Funny enough, the worst movie poster was viewed at the same time I viewed the best. Don't Tell Mom The Babysitter's Dead (1991) was a double feature with Terminator 2. Thankfully it was shown after Terminator so we left within ten minutes of the movie. I remember staring at the poster wondering what the hell was happening here? I remember bursting into tears at the poster and telling my mother I didn't like this movie. She reassured me by telling me we wouldn't have to watch it if I don't like it and sure enough we left the cinema. I've never attempted to watch it since then and it probably maybe a damn good movie but that horrid poster still brings out the scared toddler in me.

Do biracial people ever pick their white side and identify as white? Sigh The above photo shows five mixed raced men of varying ethnic makeup, myself included. Which one do you think would be the most likely to identify as ‘white?’ If you chose the guy on the far left, congratulations, you have a talent to point out the obvious. That's my cousin. We all are. He is mixed race but looks ‘white.’ Growing up he never picked his white side, society picked it for him. Trinidad has a very small ‘Caucasian’ minority and as such he has been identified as one by the public and has grown to accept and embrace that identification. In the real world nobody wants to hear what you identify yourself as. You don't pick whether you are white or black, society does. If you try to challenge society’s label and argue that you are white when you look black or that you are black when you look white, you end up losing a lot of time, wasting a lot of energy and not to mention, irritating a lot of people with a topic that is intrinsically pointless. So whether you identify as white, black, male, female, young, old, binary, non-binary, here's some news for you: No one cares. No one is really listening. Nothing has changed.

What local delicacy in your country would horrify most foreigners? Iguana Eggs I'm open minded to strange foods but when a co-worker offered me a taste of her iguana egg lunch, I had to reject her offer with more diplomacy than a politician. Iguanas in Trinidad are a common delicacy in rural areas. Curried iguana is the most frequent way of preparing it. I would guess that the meal became popular because iguanas are not the brightest animals in the reptile kingdom. They always get stuck in fences and love to take the path that makes contact with human civilization. Someday I'll venture to consume an iguana egg but for now if one of the critters get caught in my fence I'll be the odd guy who frees it.

Did you ever stop caring about how old you are? I remember when I was 17 and the anxiety I felt knowing that in a few months I would be a full fledged adult with responsibilities. Ripe for work life, going steady and potential marriage. Reality: I was just a kid still going to school and nothing remotely resembling a girlfriend. I remember when I was 19 how much the prospect of turning 20 meant. The big 2–0 meant that I was a ‘hardback’ man planning his career, house and family. No time for shits and giggles. Reality: This was the most immature period of my life and I was far from any kind of career, house or family. I had more time than ever for shits and giggles. I remember at 25 I observed my hairline beginning to recede. I was paranoid that I was going bald. I felt like I would be seen as a balding old perv if I chatted up 18 yo girls in the mall. I thought I was no longer a youth. Reality: I was not a balding old perv but a young man with self esteem issues. At 30 I was working two jobs trying to make ends meet. I had a daughter and was in a troubled relationship with her mother. The last thing I cared about was how old I was and I haven’t put much thought to it since almost seven years later. The moral of my story is I would’ve enjoyed my life much better if I didn’t worry about age and age expectations the way I did as a youth. I am much less bothered about turning 40 than when I was about to turn 20. When the time comes I’ll be proud to know that I was lucky to live so long.

What is your review of The Banshees of Inisherin? Watched this last Saturday with my girlfriend who thought it looked fascinating. Reading the two other reviews I agree with both as they mention that as a film it remains with you. To this hour it is still slowly digesting into my subconscious. I must stress on the word slow though. That is one of the biggest issues I had with the film. There's slow burner, where something is supposed to happen to connect the dots and then there's just slow, where there is little to no point. It's just slow for being slow's sake. That's the case with Banshees imho. The film posits the reason for the slowness being that Inisherin is a remote isle off Ireland and it's the 1920s. There is no electricity and the isle is so dull best friends no longer speaking could make front page news. This is actually the basis of the plot. Colin Farrel's Pádraic and Brendon Gleeson's Colm are no longer on speaking terms. Pádraic wants to continue idle chatting over beers in the pub while Colm wants more in life. This sets the stage for a series of surreal events that's supposed to be a mataphor for Irish Republicanism or something or the other. It is at that point where the film started losing me slowly. The cast is great, particularly Colin Farrell's slow-witted but good natured character who reminds me of George W Bush at times. He hits the nail on the head as a middle-aged, needy, ineffectual drunk. The cinematography is pretty and it does give a genuine sense of a place lost in time exactly one century ago. However both my girlfriend and I felt as though there was really no point. In beating on the head its symbolism and satire the movie missed out on what could've been a truly good period piece. My rating ** out of 4.

Are straight men ever attracted to very feminine gay guys? I saw one of the most beautiful girls I ever saw working behind the counter at a University campus KFC. She had bright hazel eyes that lay upon a soft, small face; an innocently seductive countenance that was accentuated with a small yet stately nose that anchored a teasing mouth. She nonchalantly chewed on gum as she stared at me with a defiant gaze. Her narrow shoulders wanted the protection of a man of resolve, a clever yet ruthless man; a man like me. Her hips swished and swayed as she trotted about in a fitted black trousers that revealed her shapely legs. I felt nervous as she stared at me, eyebrows lifted, awaiting for me to say something. Her breasts……….her breasts were……………..OK she was a bit on the flat side but that face alone was enough to build a Trojan horse for. She looked so cocky. I wanted to show her how cocky I was. I was going to say something like: ‘I order you to give me your number.’ What?? That’s real psycho-rapist stuff. How about: ‘A two piece with you on the side.’ Yeah. That’s class. Ok. Say it………….no. That’s stupid. I’ll just give my order. But I’ll say it seductively. ‘Can I take your order?’ Who said that!? That voice? That tinny, cloying but clearly masculine voice; the voice of an old, curmudgeonous geezer. It felt as though the circuits in my brain sparked and scrambled. It felt as though there was a glitch in the matrix; a tear in the fabric of our universe. It made me shudder and feel paranoid. ‘Sir. Can I take your order please?’ That awful old man voice. It came from the beautiful girl in front of me. I looked at her name tag. ‘Hello. My name is Aaron.’ The most beautiful KFC maiden was a man. An emotion never experienced before; an amalgamation of revulsion, curiosity and betrayed lust made me feel like running away but keeping my eyes on her/him while running. It felt almost similar to the feeling one gets to suddenly detecting that you're being watched and scrutinized by a hidden figure; a feeling of vulnerability. I had to leave the KFC to process what the hell just happened. Did I question my sexuality? Damn right I did. I came to the verdict that I wasn’t gay but by instinct, I was wired to be attracted to feminine features. I learned that, if possible, always read someone’s name tag before you decide to lust after them.

What are the things no one tells you about living alone? That it gradually transforms you into someone who WANTS to be alone. If you are like me and have just a drop of introvert blood in you, living alone becomes like an introvert blood transfusion. Or, as I like to call it, an introversion. When you're accustomed hanging out with groups of diverse friends, hearing about the different lifestyles , perceptions and life choices of others, not only does empathy and understanding come naturally but also a desire to empathize and understand people around you grows. If you don't do this regularly, you feel awkward and incomplete. It becomes a subconscious necessity the same way people who have a gym routine tend to always have to be at the gym otherwise they'll be in an awful mood. When you live with someone your mind gravitates towards the study and understanding of the person/persons living with you. Whether it be your spouse, children, sibling, in-law, friend, roommate etc, you naturally become preoccupied studying such an individual and the gears of human nature are in motion in that you become naturally interested in people as a whole. When you live alone, your mind becomes preoccupied with itself and your own interests, likes and dislikes, theories and experiences. Your ability to empathize lessens greatly and you find yourself easily irritated and avoiding people who do not share the same mindset as yours (practically the rest of the world). You've become so used to expending energy inwards that it becomes a Herculean effort to try and get to know others. You'd rather not pretend to be glad about Megan's new boyfriend (who sounds like a piece of s**t) or grudgingly compliment Billy on his decision to take his kids to Disneyland rather than pay off his arrears for the car or be pressured into attending the church cake sale when you're secretly an atheist. Living alone makes you that person who just doesn't want to make that effort to get to know the people around you. Getting to know people seems about as difficult and exhausting as someone with physique of Gandhi trying to do the workout of a prime Arnold Schwarzenegger. Unless you are a natural recluse, living alone is not a good idea for the reasons stated above. But hey that's just my two cents.

What is that one picture that describes the lowest point in your life? Sometime in April 2015 I used to be one of those who believed that depression was a hackneyed excuse, lazy people used as a defence mechanism. I believed that any mental struggle could be conquered on a mind-over-matter basis. My extended family was prone to bouts of depression and bipolar disorder and I would always roll my eyes when I heard them speak of their troubles and how it has affected their lives. At age 28 my girlfriend became pregnant. It was not planned. Prior to this announcement we were sharing a modest apartment and no matter how much I tightened my belt I couldn't overcome experiencing great financial difficulties. Besides my day job I also got an income doing transport and lawn maintenance. Soon my vehicle started giving me no end of troubles and I could no longer spend money fixing it so I left it to rot. My credit card was maxed out and I was owing money to some of my friends. After paying rent I could barely afford groceries. My financial woes caused me to lose contact with my friends so when she and I argued (which was every week) and she stormed out, I was left destitute and lonely in a shabby apartment complex, no one and nowhere to turn. During one of these episodes, like an awful aftertaste, a notion came into my mind. You've made a big mistake. You're going to f**k this child's life up . I tried to laugh away the notion but it buzzed around my mind like some sort of devilish fairy. You’re just another deadbeat father who can't get it right. I started pacing around trying to get this notion out of my mind. My heart raced and my nerves were on edge. My head felt light and heavy at the same time. You've made such a big mistake. What the hell were you thinking? I took deep breaths and attempted to think positive thoughts. Then as though a floodgate was released, it came: panic attacks. I felt these strange sensations in my skin, these popping, spasmic sensations similar to the plastic bubbles that wrap your delivery that you pop unconsciously with your fingers. It was completely overwhelming. I sat down to try and breathe it away, mind-over-matter as I used to preach but it simply gave way to what I can only describe as the feeling of a heavy, stifling bog taking residence in my brain. It was depression. My back hunched over as my mind felt clogged and lifeless. I couldn't stop thinking of my problems and asking myself interrogative questions. I sat down in defeat, fearful for anyone to see me like this, fearful for the phone to ring. The worst thing about depression is that it tricks you into believing that your life was always a series of tragedy and sorrow, that this is how things are and has always been. It was as though my positive emotions and memories were locked away in a cellar, unrecognizable in an iron mask. I felt like a burden and a drain on other people's happiness. When I saw other people happy and proactive it only reminded me of how unhappy and useless I was. These sensations would usually happen during sunsets for some strange reason. My appetite was all but gone so was my passions and interests. At its peak I became emaciated, 30–40 pounds lighter than my usual self. This feeling came on a daily basis, first with a dose of panic attacks then sinking into that low, rotting, depressed feeling where my face literally looked like Eeyore from Winnie the Pooh. I would record my suicidal feelings on a rating from 1 to 10 and on many days I would record myself as high as 9. After my daughter was born I was terrified of getting the male version of post partum depression. Thankfully, I was lucky, the depression wasn't chronic and it waned to a point where only once a week I got those horrid familiar feelings but of a lesser intensity. After a year I was healthy enough to take up a second job, clear my debts and provide for my daughter whilst my mental demons were held at bay. Today, I am in a much better place mentally and financially. Not going to brag but I think I've accomplished a bit since depression first reared its ugly head seven years ago. However, it's comes back every now and again. Like a unwanted vagabond it shows up at my doorstep, bedraggled and defeated, but not yet dead and it stops me in my tracks to give me a taste of those familiar feelings of the past, (usually during sunsets). Depression is no joke. If you know someone who demonstrates any symptoms/behaviours such as I had/did, try your best to assist that person, without overwhelming them with pity and making a huge fuss. Be patient with such a person without coming across as though they are helpless. Just play it cool. Edit 21.01.22. Depression and other mental illnesses play a great role in relationships and with families. It is very difficult to be in a relationship with a spouse who suffers from mental illness. It can cause severe problems for future generations. Click here to read how it.

What are the cleverest scams you have come across? Take a breath, grab a coffee if you may, and allow me to explain to you why we are called 'Tricky-dadians’ by the rest of the Caribbean. Band Ladies Around 2016 — 2018 a phenomenon occurred where sightings of these cultish ladies in heavy clothing similar to that of traditional Amish females were found throughout Trinidad. They were typically spotted at commercial areas such as malls and PriceSmarts (Costco) mostly at the parking lot. They were renowned for asking for your assistance with the rebuilding of their church. They claimed to do this with the purchase of their cheap rubber hand bands of which they would charge anything upwards of $20TT. If you refused to buy their generic, overpriced bands they would then initiate Phase 2 of their scheme which would be to overwhelm the victim with guilt with a pathos laden statement of 'Or maybe you could contribute just a small donation. Anything?’ They employed great acting skills and for many, seeing these harmless women in humble, old fashioned garb being constantly refused and rejected for their worthy cause tugged a few heartstrings. However, as with most scams, they got too greedy too fast. Their monthly appearances soon turned to weekly and then daily. Rather than target one location for the day and wrap up afterwards, it soon became clear that they began employing routes. A typical Band Lady route would be PriceSmart Chaguanas till 2pm, Trincity Mall until 6pm and PriceSmart Mausica until 9pm. They were noticed and mentioned by some of the populace but being that they were always pleasant and took 'no’ graciously, no one bothered to think twice about their scheme. However, the last straw was a rather desperate appearance at a CPL T20 cricket match (above photograph). Trinidad is very tolerant of beggars and we throw a blind eye towards scammers for the most part but for the Band Ladies, plying their scheme in the middle of a regional cricket match where national pride was at a peak, created an online outcry. Everyone suddenly posted a story, photo or recording of a dubious encounter with one of these Band Ladies and from that moment on they were no longer seen in public. Warning *Foul language*

What is the stupidest assumption you ever made? Several years ago I worked as a warehouse attendant for a major distribution company. It was my first job. Every year, usually in September, we had our annual stock-taking exercise. It was bittersweet because though it was hard work (especially for the males who did all the climbing and counting every single product in the warehouse whilst females wrote figures on the notepad) there would usually be a lot of the beautiful Head Office women present and we would be treated to lunch by the Director. We were all randomly assigned one partner. On our notice board they would put the name of our randomly allocated mystery partner. Of course many of the virile and single young men like myself hoped and prayed to be partnered with a stunning beauty from the Head Office. When the list was put up I saw that my partner was ‘Vanessa Milan.’ I jumped high into the air in excitement. VANESSA MILAN What a name! I envisioned a tanned beauty from a Mediterranean island, tall and shapely with arched eyebrows, a sensuous mouth and curly jet, black hair. In other words I imagined a Sophia Loren look-alike. I began bragging to my male friends that Vanessa Milan and I would probably be secretly in each others arms embracing behind a pallet of goods whilst they would be walking on eggshells with their nagging, old-maid partners. Every time I mentioned Vanessa Milan’s name I said it in a low whisper as though she were the Latin Goddess of Forbidden Love. ‘Vanessa Milan’ I drove my co-workers crazy uttering her exotic name every day. ‘Vanessa Milan’ I laughed at some of the names my friends were paired with: ‘Penny Thomas….Ha…..That sounds like a big, fat mama.’ ‘Giselle Aleong….she sounds like a bony psycho.’ And comments to that extent (I was 19 years old). One of my friends Rory advised me that I was a fool. That nothing could be more stupid than guessing what someone is like based on their name. I replied, ‘True, But a name like Vanessa Milan has to be an exotic beauty. Who ever heard a name like Vanessa Milan in this country?’ When the day came for the stock-take, all of us guys stood in the open area of the warehouse and observed a wide array of beauties from the Head Office. The Director gathered us all together for a prayer and then called out the names of the allocated partners for us to team up. Penny Thomas was a straight up knock-out. Giselle Aleong, with a body like that, could’ve graced the cover of Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Edition. I looked stunned as she walked by with my friend Rory (her assigned partner) who had warned me about my assumptions. He looked at me with a faint, mocking smile. When Vanessa Milan’s name was called, (the Director blasphemously screeched her name in her guttural voice) no one answered. All my friends stared at me as they were in great suspense to finally see this exotic mystery woman I boasted about all week. Suddenly, a dumpy, middle-aged lady with bad posture and Coke bottle specs that made her look like someone’s mom from the 60’s came hurriedly into the clearing. ‘I’m here. I’m here,’ she cried in a mournful voice. I was taken aback. Sophia Loren she wasn’t. She looked and acted more like Pat from the It’s Pat SNL sketch. Awkwardly I shook hands with her and stared at the ground. She began to relate a woeful tale of how she wasn’t feeling well that morning and was running late as she sped up the road driving but had forgotten to feed her dog so she had to drive back home and that was why she was late and on and on and on she went relating woeful, semi-depressing tales for me while we were doing our stock checks. ‘One hundred and seventy five cases of Diquez Baby Oil 125ml!’ I shouted down at her from a pallet of goods on the shelf above her, ‘Did you get that?’ ‘Oh sorry,’ she said, ‘I can’t hear you. I have bad hearing in my right ear. Ever since I was…..’ ‘ONE-SEVEN-FIVE CASES……DIQUEZ BABY OIL…….125ML, ‘ I shouted at the top of my lungs. This was the third time in thirty minutes this type of communication problem happened and I was getting frustrated. Part of it was my selfish and immature disappointment at her not being the beauty I imagined but alas she was so whiny and helpless. ‘I can’t hear you.’ she replied woefully, ‘I think we should go ask the Director if the Manager has any walky-talkies around.’ ‘WE DON’T HAVE ANY WALKY-TALKIES IN THE WAREHOUSE,’ I screamed at her but she already left to find the Director while I stood suspended 30 feet above the ground on a shelf waiting on her. In the end I had to count the stock and write in the figures myself as she followed me about apologizing at every turn. After the momentous day passed, for weeks my friends and co-workers would tease me. They would breathlessly whisper her name whenever I passed. ‘Vanessa Milan. Mi amore. Mi amore.’ Thus ended the saga of Vanessa Milan, My Latin Goddess of Forbidden Love.

What was a red flag that made you stop talking to a person immediately? My brother had a relative staying over at his apartment and she brought along a friend. They both had just turned 18 and had recently run off from home (Red Flag #1) and were crashing at my brother's place basically sleeping all day and partying all night to their teenaged wont. I struck up a conversation with the friend (let's just call her Alice for simplicity's sake) and found her quite intelligent and charming despite her lifestyle. Went with Alice to hang out one night and we ended up in a club. We began dancing but I was quite surprised how physically close she positioned herself while we danced as we had only just met a week ago (Red Flag #2). I then asked her about how it was staying with my brother and she began a slew of insults as towards my brother's manners and housekeeping standards (Red Flag #3) despite the fact that she didn't help with his bills or rent. We exchanged numbers and I dropped her off home. She laid on her charm quite thick the entire journey and spoke of how great of a guy I was and that she couldn't wait for us to chat again. We exchanged numbers and the following morning I called her to see how she was doing. In a groggy voice she said ‘Who is this?’ I told her my name and to my surprise she said in a irritated tone, ‘Who? How did you get my number?’ (Red Flag #4) I reminded her that she gave me her number willingly the night before. She tried to laugh it off as being hung over. I reminded her that she only had one drink last night (Red Flag #5). There was an awkward silence and she tried to coo about how great of a guy I was but I cut her short and said that I was getting another call. Three years later Alice got pregnant for her boyfriend's married boss.

What is the strangest thing a truck driver has seen while driving? I'm cheating a bit. It was a pickup truck but I was hauling a long distance furniture delivery so technically it still counts. My loader Chris and I were on the highway when suddenly a spooked chicken ran across the road in front of us. I'm a soft hearted person by nature so my first instinct was to try and avoid it. As if reading my mind, Chris sternly told me to hit it. He had always advised me that, while driving full speed on the highway, never try to avoid hitting animals that step in front of you, be it a cat, dog or bird. He knew of people who got killed in smash ups trying to avoid hitting the random stray dog on the highway. I did as he advised and the chicken collided with the pick up at a velocity that surely killed it. ‘Pull to the side’ said Chris. He wanted to collect the dead bird to clean and cook when he got home later. I did as told, parked on the shoulder and reversed closer to where the dead bird lay. Chris got out to retrieve his spoils but after a minute he came back with an odd look on his face. ‘What?’ I said. He told me that I needed to see it for myself. I went with him to the bird and looked at it. Everything looked alright. Except for the fact that the bird was in a state whereby it had to have been dead for several hours. Its face and skin had that grey look of being long dead and there were ants coming out of its beak and an eyeless socket. ‘This can't be the chicken that we hit!’ I said. ‘It has to be another chicken that we hit! This one's already dead.’ Chris demonstrated to me that this was the exact location where we struck the chicken. There were feathers that got dislodged from the impact nearby that matched with our speckled bird. It was indeed our chicken. ‘This doesn't make any sense.’ I said stupified. Chris didn't think much about it. He was more focused on the disappointment that his roadkill was inedible. Zombie chickens crossing the road didn't seem to be of any concern to him. To this day I have no idea as to what could poossibly explain that supernatural event.

Who is the creepiest guy you've ever met? It happened just last week! I don't know if he's the creepiest guy I've ever met but he probably ranks in the top 5. It was a Thursday night at Papa John's and I had just came back from a delivery. As I entered the store my eyes met with a large man with greying dreadlocks tied in a ponytail. He appeared in his mid to late 40s. He was sweating profusely. This was remarkable given the fact that the restaurant was quite cold to the point that customers would continuously ask us to take off the front unit. It's hard to explain the unsettling feeling I felt when our eyes met. I had to look away immediately. I swear he gave me the look that vicious dogs give when they are contemplating whether to tear you to shreds. I try not to judge people by just looking at them but in this case I went to the supervisor and queried as to whether that guy's pizza was finished. 'Why?’ she replied. 'He gives me a bad feeling,' I said. We both looked over at him for a second but had to stop looking because he was unflinchingly staring at us and his mouth was slightly quivering as though he was using all his energy to restrain himself. His veggie pizza was finished and we both argued as to who should hand him his order when suddenly a young couple with their 5 year old daughter came to order. I had a nice excuse to lay the guy's pizza on the counter and quickly evade any communication with him by attending to the new customers. I did just so, beckoned the guy by nodding towards him and went to the family who were ready to order. While I was taking their order the father made a corny joke that he wanted a pizza with every possible topping added to it. I feigned a laugh when suddenly the big, bulking creepster comes over and in an angry voice he bellows, 'Every ingredient? You must be rich. You must be Papa John himself.’ The creepster begins to laugh in a coarse, loud and unsettling manner. Both myself and the father feigned laughing with him. 'Pizza man!’ the creepster literally shouts while looking me square in the eyes. He says those two words as though he was really saying, 'You're next.’ 'Tell the man you want $50,000 f**king dollars to make that pizza.’ Creepster makes an ominous belly chuckle that was seemingly neverending and the little girl looks terrified. It was clear that the man was deranged and quite possible dangerous. Being a man of the world, the father attempts to nullify the guy by making everything seem normal. 'What you ordered there brother?’ 'Veggie,' the creepster replies, 'I'm a rasta so no meat for me. Except for the p***y I'm going to be eating later.’ As though to ensure he is as offensive as possible the creepster repeats that last statement, as though to ensure the little girl hears him and gives his hideous laugh while he exits. Myself and the family look at one another in both a state of relief and disbelief but decide not to mention anything. That had to have been the creepiest incident I've had all year. I know that many times people who have a horrible outward appearance can in fact be really nice people and vice versa but in this case I am certain that that guy had the potential to do evil, if he had not done so already. I really hope he didn't like our pizza.

Has your friend ever saved your life? Well he's my cousin but he's also my friend. Ten years ago my cousin Keeghan and I were staying at his family's beach house. Feeling idle we decided to roam the empty beach an early morning, light cherry bombs and fling them in random directions. The beach (Las Cuevas) was long and we walked the entire length towards the west. It ended at some cliffs and we spotted a large smooth surfaced rock several feet from the shore. I watched as my 6′5 cousin swam to it and climbed to the top. I immediately followed suit. However my luck was it that strong winds had the waves lashing against the rock generating some strong, swirling undercurrents. As I reached towards the rock I felt the undercurrent pull me downwards, spun me around and flung me upwards. I laughed it off and so did Keeghan. He said I looked like a lump of shit being flushed. As I began laughing the undercurrent pulled me down again and kept me swirling underwater. I had to utilize energy to avoid slamming into the rock while being tossed around. As hard as I tried to break out of the swirling undercurrents it was too strong and I only managed to tire myself out. Keeghan saw that I was beginning to gurgle and lose energy, it was only a matter of time before I drowned. He jumped into the water in an area where the water wasn't swirling and being blessed with a long frame he was able to easily reach me and pull me out of the undercurrent. We laughed it off and he played it like no big deal but I knew that I would've been dead if it wasn't for him.

Was Shelley Duvall considered attractive? When I was a boy growing up, this character was the epitome of ‘attractive’ among boys my age: This was the exact opposite: Now that I'm a full grown adult I find it odd that my attraction has reversed. Nowadays I would consider prime Shelley Duvall far more attractive than prime Pamela Anderson. I'm not saying this as a form of virtue signalling due to her sad passing. I've observed photos from her in the past and discovered that she possessed a very unique beauty. This beauty was exploited quite often in her roles and modeling in the 1970s. Sadly she was only given frumpy housewife and plain Jane supporting roles into the 80s and 90s and all but disappeared at the turn of the millenium, only resurfacing for that infamous Dr. Phil interview in 2016. Despite being tall and thin, with big ears and eyes and crooked teeth Shelley Duvall’s looks were all natural. This might be my personal opinion but she seemed to possess a certain humility about her; the kind of person who wouldn't put on airs about herself and be friendly to almost anyone. Pamela Anderson’s beauty involved a lot of plastic surgery, hair dye and excessive makeup. To each his own but in a hypothetical party full of people I'd make a bee line to be the first to offer a drink to Shelley Duvall. Then we'd talk, sit and laugh at all the hopelessly shallow guys flocking around Pamela Anderson at the other end of the room. RIP

Who was the rudest person you’ve ever encountered? And what was your response? Some years ago I was working the late shift at my part time job doing pizza delivery. I was taking phone calls when a smug, off-putting voice was suddenly heard on the other end of the line. 'Are you hearing me? This is Michael Griffith. G-r-i-f-f-i-t-h.’ There was a second of silence as I registered that that the person didn't even bother to say 'Good Evening.’ I acknowledged that I could hear him and subtly mentioned that I could spell. I then proceeded to ask him for more information. 'I have been a regular customer to this restaurant for over 15 years. I like my pizzas done a special way. Are you listening……what is your name?’ 'Elijah sir.’ 'I want a veggie pizza. Listen to how I want it……Are you hearing me?……..I want the dough baked with the pizza sauce and cheese, nothing else added………are you writing this down?…….Then I want the raw veggies added after the pizza has been cooked. DO NOT COOK MY VEGGIES. I REPEAT. DO NOT COOK THE VEGGIES ON MY PIZZA.’ I tried my best to separate this man's condescending tone and my feelings towards him and mentally process exactly what it was he requested. We always got customers who felt entitled to have their pizza done in some special way. Either they wanted their pizza baked separate from all other pizzas or their dough must be of a certain grade or the pineapples must be cut from fresh fruit and not from our canned stock. Most of the time we ignored them and just gave them what they (and everyone else) were paying for. Most of the time they just wanted to feel bourgeois. This guy however was adamant that I make his pizza with raw veggies. What this guy didn't seem to realize was that these veggies were never freshly cut veggies. These were precut veggies sitting overnight in a plastic tub in a chiller, probably swarming with bacterial matter. Cooking these veggies in the oven was his only defense against E-coli. If he were to get sick from eating his beloved raw veggie pizza, he could hold us accountable and sue and I would be the one to get the blame. I diplomatically expressed to him that we couldn't make his pizza in such a manner, that it was a risk to his health and against the company's policy. In anger he asked for my name a second time. 'Listen to me young man. I am arriving in 15 minutes and if I do not see my veggie pizza prepared the way I want it, I am going to deal with you.’ He then hung up the phone. I explained what just happened to the cashier and she agreed with me that the guy was an idiot and that we couldn't give him a raw veggie pizza. I processed the pizza order as a regular veggie pizza and continued taking calls. Fifteen minutes later I'm in the back, about to head out on a delivery when I heard a smug but familiar voice bellowing out at front counter, 'WHERE'S THAT STUPID BOY NIGEL?’ I looked in front to see Mr. E-coli in the flesh. He looked exactly like how I imagined he would look; large, big-bellied and bespectacled. He was middle aged and greying, with a thick bottom lip that projected outwards in perpetual disgust at the world in front of him. I kid you not he looked like the human version of the obnoxious character Bubble Bass from SpongeBob. Immediately my entire physique and mental structure took to the offense. I literally wanted to clobber this idiot. However, I marched to the front counter to confront him and use all my powers of vocabulary to diplomatically explain to him that he was an idiot and that he was not getting a raw veggie pizza from this branch. As if to make himself as repulsive as ever, with him was a preteen girl (either his niece or daughter) with whom he tried to exaggerate how tough he was, by yelling and berating, mostly female minimum wage paid fast food workers. 'Listen to me,' he shouted at the cashier, 'Remove this pizza and get me what I ordered. I want to see that boy who took my order.’ He then spread a creepy smile over his face, turned to the little girl and cooed, 'You’re gonna taste the real way to eat pizza.’ The poor little girl looked like she wished she could disappear at the moment. Everything about the guy was just so off-putting in an incongruent sense. He was like a living, breathing 'Can you find all the things wrong in this picture’ cartoon brought to life. 'I'm the one who took your order sir,’ I said with seething rage as he glanced me, ‘And you can't get a raw veggie pizza.’ I saw him turn red. This was no longer about the pizza. This was about him proving himself to that little girl. 'You telling me what I can or can't get?’ he bellowed, 'You want me to knock you out?’ I stood there waiting for the tub of lard to attack when the manager flew out her office and came between us. In her best prepared monologue she explained she was sorry for his inconvenience. The manager told me to go to the back. In anger I listened as she explained the danger of consuming such a pizza but acquiesced to his demand. After I cooled down some minutes later I grabbed a delivery and en route to my motorcycle out front I spotted him shovelling away his bacteria ridden pizza in his mouth and commanding the little girl to do the same. He gave me a nervous sideglance as I passed, then continued goading her to finish her slice. I asked God to protect that little girl from getting sick and pleaded that He not allow more idiots like that man to multiply on this Earth.

What screams "I'm low class"? A girl, no older than 20 comes into Papa John's a busy Friday evening. I'm helping out at the cash register. It's near the end of the month (pay day for most people) and this is when we get our bulk of orders. The phone is ringing off the hook. I'm really just a delivery guy but the store is short staffed so I help cash. The girl, her cellphone tucked at her groin area in her trousers comes up to me at the register. Totally ignoring the fact that I'm taking an order on the phone she proceeds to talk about what she wants. I paused from the phone call to tell her, ‘One minute please miss I'm on the phone with a customer.’ I look as her eyebrows slant further downwards in anger and she puts her arms on her hips, staring at me in a show of impatience. When I finished with the call I apologized and asked what would she like. ‘Gimme one of the chicken pizzas.’ The phone started ringing again. I sighed inwardly. All the time she spent staring at me in anger she didn't even make up her mind as to what she wanted. ‘Which one of the chicken pizzas?’ I don't know if by asking a simple question like that she found some measure of offense but she replied in a belligerent tone, ‘How am I supposed to know what chicken pizzas you have?’ The phone continued ringing. I sighed again. I pointed to the display above her head and told her I have to take the call, choose a pizza by the time. Instead she frowns at me while I take another phone order, she refusing to look at the menu board herself. When I was done she glared at me and said, ‘Chicken and pine….the largest size you have.’ ‘That would be an extra large’ I said. ‘I know!’ she spat. She then proceeds to take out of her purse a brown envelope which contained the salary she just received from whatever job she worked. She proudly counts her 100s in front of me and gave me $200 without waiting for me to tell her the price of her order. I gave her her change and receipt and told her the waiting time (15–20 mins). She proceeded to stare at me whilst I take other orders, helped cut pizzas from off the oven and organized my deliveries at the same time. With her seeing me doing all these things at once I thought she would have generated some sympathy for me seeing that I wasn't really the cashier but just a delivery guy helping out the situation. While heading towards the exit with my deliveries I passed near her and she beckons me. I thought it was to apologize for her attitude. Instead she tells me something that makes my blood boil instantly. ‘Ummm. How much longer for my order?’ She just placed her order 5 minutes ago! I gritted me teeth and replied, ‘It’s not in the oven yet. 10 to 15 minutes.’ She rolled her eyes and looked away. I then realize what her game was. She didn't really care about the pizza. Her fetish was to feel some sort of superiority over someone else and the only place she could achieve that was in a fast food restaurant. We get customers like that regularly, especially around month's end (pay day). They get some kind of sick thrill out of pissing people off and flaunting what (little) money they have. So to answer the question above, nothing screams 'I’m low class’ more than people who buy fast food for the sake of showing off/putting on airs.

Who are the most uncomfortable movie characters depicting the UK that you’ve ever seen? Gotta go with three films and I'm listing the characters based on the level of discomfort (low to high). *** Spoilers ahead *** Movie: Saturday Night and Sunday Morning (1960) Character(s): Arthur Location: Nottingham The late, great Albert Finney gives a magnificent performance as Arthur, a rebellious, young, working class man who has somewhat of a fetish for stirring up trouble and going beyond the limit. The title refers to the fact that Arthur begins his trouble immediately after his work ends on Saturday. He dedicates his Saturday nights to going out pubs and drinking himself beyond consciousness, stirring up trouble in the streets, fighting etc. His Sundays are spent engaging in a sexual affair with the equally defiant wife of his mild-mannered co-worker. He eventually gets her pregnant while hiding his deeds from his own morally virtuous girlfriend. In the final scene Arthur confesses his actions to his girlfriend who forgives him and gets him to agree to marry her and settle down. Arthur agrees but angrily throws a stone at a nearby building. His girlfriend asks 'What did you do that for?’ He replies, 'Just felt like it I suppose.’ I don't live in the UK but I know and have befriended many Arthurs throughout my life here in Trinidad. Arthurs can never find inner peace and unknowingly to themselves, foster a subconscious hatred towards structure, routine and normalcy. They believe that a stone must be thrown into the rolling cogs every so often otherwise life would just be uneventful and monotonous. At their best Arthurs can be just angry, resentful troublemakers but at their worst they can be psychopathic narcissists who cause harm and destruction to all those who engage with them. Arthur in this film was a downright bastard in this kitchen-sink classic and anyone not interested in him as a character study would simply find him mildly repugnant. Movie: Kill List (2011) Character(s): Jay Location: Sheffield Kill List is something of a psychological/supernatural horror inspired by the fiction of HP Lovecraft. However there's nothing fictional about the character Jay. He's a menacing, angry and uncouth ex-soldier turned contract killer, quite possibly suffering from PTSD from a botched mission. He has a son and a wife who urges him to take a normal job as they are in financial distress but Jay prefers to wait for that one big contract job that would provide for him for years to come. His 'luck’ arrives as a friend of his wife hires him to eliminate various unnamed people in a mysterious Kill List. Jay and his friend are given locations of the targets The Priest, The Librarian and The MP. Each kill becomes more mysterious than the last with both of the first two victims softly thanking Jay before being killed. The 2nd kill unearths video evidence of an underground society involved in the most, depraved and disturbing acts imaginable causing Jay to become even more unsettled. Jay's final kill leads him to a mansion where a some sort of pagan cult is taking place with several figures hidden in white robes are having a ceremony. Believing these to be the people involved in the depraved videos he starts shooting them, killing some and manages to kill the leader. However he is captured and forced to a knife-fight with a robed hunchback figure. Viciously stabbing the hunchback all over its body, it is revealed afterwards to be his wife with their son strapped to her back. His final kill was his own family. I believe Kill List to be a portrayal of a man with psychosis and schizophrenia brought on by severe PTSD. Neil Maskell gives a phenomenal performance as Jay. His consistently scowling face and venemous tone make him such an unsettling character that I fear ever running into such a person on a lonely side street at night. I may be wrong but I interpret a lot of the happenings to be solely in Jay's imagination. Jay saw his own killings as something as a grand mission against evil so as to erase guilt from a botched mission in Kyiv where he, quite possibly, had to do heinous acts to survive. Kill List, to me, is a heightened portrayal of a mentally unstable man. Movie: Eden Lake (2008) Character(s): The parents Location: London Condemned by critics for stereotyping and exaggerating the 'Broken Britain’ underclass this film is relentless in its portrayal of savagery. Jenny and Steve are a couple vacationing and decide a visit a lake near a working class community. Steve is highly critical of the behaviour of the children of the area and the parents' role in their poor upbringing. Even though the lake is condemned to become a quarry Steve and Jenny sneak in for a final visit but become targets of a gang of local delinquent 'Chavs’ driven by a maniacal leader Brett. After constantly being harassed by the youths, a fight ensues in which Brett's dog is killed. Enraged he eventually raises the stakes by capturing Steve and having members of the group stab him to death while being filmed. Jenny is then captured and with botched attempts to kill her as well, Brett murders two of his own gang members while the rest look on silently. In the ensuing chase two other members of the gang are killed. Bleeding to near death and dirty, Jenny manages to run to a nearby house where a house party involving several middle aged locals are taking place. There is copious drug, alcohol and sex among the members and even though it is certain that these people are not her cup of tea she seeks help from one of the more sympathetic women. However she soon realises that many of them are parents of the gang and when one of the women get a police call informing of her murdered son, the parents suspect her and suddenly transform into 'we look after our own’ monsters. As far fetched as Brett and the gang is portrayed, I believe a good job was done portraying the parents. There are so many communities of families out there who have vague morals in regards to greater society but a strict code of secrecy and loyalty for themselves. Despite many of the horrific scenes in the movie, nothing was more uncomfortable and disturbing than this final scene. There is no major onscreen violence during the last five minutes but just looking at Jenny hiding in the bathroom as she hears the voices of the parents of these monsters (learning of their dead kids) screaming in trauma and yelling in rage as she acknowledges the fact that they will soon kill her makes it the most uncomfortable scene I've ever witnessed in a film set in the UK.

What movies with interesting concepts were poorly executed? Looper (2012) ***Spoilers ahead*** Looper has the distinction of one of those rare movies. In the beginning it reminds me of why I love Hollywood and in the end it reminds me of why I hate Hollywood. Big budget Hollywood has mastered the art of dishing out movies that build imaginative concepts and develops intriguing characters and then by the halfway mark s**ts all over it with mindless action, tepid romance, explosions and low brow sci-fi for the sake of attracting all the Beavises and Buttheads out there. The story deals with bounty hunters who kill without discretion, victims sent from an agency in the future. The very same bounty hunters have an expiry date whereby when they reach a certain age they themselves are sent back to the past to be exterminated to 'close the loop.' Many times their own past selves are the ones who do such an extermination. Fascinating concept, and it gets even more fascinating when Bruce Willis' character escapes extermination from his younger self (Joseph Gordon Levitt) and then seeks to exterminate the guy who started this whole time travel assassination agency (The Rainmaker) while avoiding being killed by himself and several other 'loopers.’ Yeah rock on. Then somehow the movie takes us to a farm with some annoying kid and his mom, some soul searching and romance is flung into the mix, throw in a bunch of boring exposition, random telekinesis and super powers and the suddenly the movie turns into The Terminator meets Akira fanfiction. By the time the movie drew to a close (Joseph Gordon Levitt kills himself to eliminate his older self….big surprise) I yearn for the day time travel could be an actual possibility, so I could undo the precious time I wasted on this overrated movie.

Have you ever been seen naked by somebody or saw somebody naked accidentally? I rented a ratty, hole in the wall apartment for a brief period when I went to University. I say ratty because the very first night I moved in I opened my door later to see a huge rat scampering off behind some junk near the wall. It was an old building that was sectioned off into a few rooms which in time were further subdivided into smaller rooms. It was like a barracks but ugly, poorly designed and devoid of any taste whatsoever. The entire upstairs and downstairs each shared one tiny kitchen and one bathroom area. I wondered what was the need for a door to the bathroom when there was a gap from the door to the door frame that was so wide you could peep in and see clearly anyone who was having a bath or a shit. As one could imagine it was rented solely by lesser income bracket males. It was a common to see tasteless, junky buildings such as this in any highly populated area in Trinidad. Practically zero laws were enforced in regards to building code so it seemed as though the owners were all competing to build the biggest, ugliest brick and mortar ant-nest in the world. The neighbouring building was no exception but it was a larger, newer and much more spacious apartment complex. The apartment was rented by students who clearly belonged to upper middle class families. The large spacious building was so tall and stately that it seemed to look down on our decrepit little hovel like a deformed, underdeveloped sibling. One night as I lay on my thin mattress, deciding whether to bear with the heat of the poorly ventilated cell-like room or open the window and bear with the plague of mosquitoes waiting patiently to enter I heard a noise that resonated in my ears and in my groin. It was the sound of female laughter. It wasn't just any laughter. It was the lusty, playful laughter of a pair of attractive young women. I looked at the window and saw an open door from the second floor apartment next door and from inside the door the well lit room revealed a girl walking several times past the door completely naked. One could imagine how a lonely, young, hot-blooded male cramped in a tiny room without a single form of entertainment at his disposal would feel to see this tender female figure darting back and forth in front of his eyes without a thread of clothing. It was like seeing flashes of heaven. I quickly turned off my lights so the girl wouldn't catch me peeping and I rooted myself by the window, hungry for more. However nothing else happened and the door closed. The following evening I was home at night trying to read a book on Investments when my ears pricked. The familiar sound of laughter could be heard. Almost on instinct I flew to my light switch and turned it off. I went to the window. This time two girls darted back and forth, nude, in front of the door. I wondered if I was dreaming. At one point, one of them stood by the doorway for several seconds, looking at her phone, allowing one to absorb the view of her body. ‘Somebody’s going to see us,’ one of them said and the mischievous nymphs laughed heartily. They both couldn't be older than 20 and from the way they interacted they were quite possibly related. It was obvious that they both enjoyed exhibition. This was not an accident. I looked at my watch. It was 6:45pm. It was around this time yesterday that one of them gave their show. Immediately the door closed for the night. The show was over. At 6:30 the following evening I was like a perverted sentry posted at my windowsill in the darkness, resolute on catching a third viewing. I wished to God I had had the means to buy binoculars. Why couldn't I been born to a well off family and living in the apartment next to them? I saw them as they came from their classes, heading towards their apartment; a pair of Indian girls, bespectacled and quite innocent looking the way they postured themselves and wore rather baggy, unbecoming clothes. In attire they were completely different creatures, almost nerdy. They looked the dictionary image of graduates from an all girls’ Convent school. They both appeared somber and reticent. They dragged themselves forward without a word to one another and went indoors, closing the door behind them halfway. What was with the moodiness? Did someone report them? Did their family find out about their exhibitions and issued a stern warning? Did someone record them and circulated their nude videos around campus? I hoped to God not. In my steaming little hovel I was hungry for more. I could hear them arguing about something for a few seconds. I could hear them laughing. I could hear them eating. I could hear the dishes being washed and packed away. C’mon! I looked at my watch. It was a minute or so before 7pm. Was tonight going to be a no-show? As the thought came to mind the door opened and the younger girl stepped forward staring at her phone, naked as the Sahara. She stood for a few seconds, myself completely succumbed in lust. The other girl shouted to her to close the door and she made a sad face as if to say, ‘Sorry for the late show but it's over now’ and she closed the door. I took a deep breath and went outside my apartment. I hoped that somehow one of them would see me through their window and feel the urge to have a conversation with me. The only thing interested in me were the mosquitoes so I quickly went back inside. I turned on my lights. Suddenly I noticed that practically every apartment that faced the girls had had their lights off and were turning them on as well. Obviously I wasn't the only one in my apartment building aware of their nightly exhibitions. On day four I took my place by the window with the lights off around 6:30pm. It was the last Friday of the month. Before I could make myself comfortable I saw the door swing wide open. Instead of my two naked nymphs I saw a tall, stern looking middle aged man carrying out a pair of suitcases. While he went out the apartment two young men who were probably his sons came and retrieved several of the the girls’ heavier belongings. As the young men left, my nymphs came out the door each holding light items. They were moving out. Based on the friendly banter among all of them it was clear that their evening exhibitionism was not a factor in their moving out. I felt heartbroken. I wanted to believe that their evening shows were for me and me only and it was only a matter of time before some form of communication took place between us. Instead they gave a good three day show and now they were gone. I wanted to find some kind of reason or excuse to go up to them and talk. ‘Do you guys need some help?’ Then I imagined their tall, stern faced father/uncle glaring at me with a murderous look and shaking his head. ‘We’re good. Thanks.’ I turned on the lights and peered at them boldly from my window. I wanted them to at least see me. The younger one was passing out the apartment and spotted me. She gave me a long curious stare while she walked and came across her sister/cousin and she began whispering in her ear and they both stopped and looked at me and then giggled. Feeling like a creep I drew back the curtains and came out of view. What now? Maybe they would stop by and say their goodbyes? Maybe I was just being pathetic? I lay in bed trying to ignore my conflicting feelings. In the shared kitchen I suddenly heard voices. Some of the boys in my apartment were hanging out or ‘liming’ as we call it here in Trinidad. They were talking about the girls who left and apparently one of them finally confided about seeing them naked at nights and they all started sharing stories of the girls’ daily naked ritual. Funny how they all never said a word to one another prior to this shared witnessing. They started some scuttlebutt on the identity of the girls and stories they heard about them from friends.
