Outside I could hear a scuttling noise. The rat was making his rounds looking for fresh garbage. The rat was a much more industrious and respectable fellow than all of us humans who allowed the sight of two naked girls to turn us into primal beasts. I decided to call it a night.

What actor or actress got cast in a role that they normally wouldn't play and absolutely crushed it? Everyone I know who saw Along Came Polly (2004) agrees that the standout comedic performance was… not Ben Stiller (The Ben Stiller Show, There's Something About Mary, Meet The Parents etc) nor Jennifer Aniston (Friends, Office Space, Bruce Almighty) nor Hank Azaria (The Simpsons, Futurama, Mystery Men) nor Debra Messing (Will and Grace, Ned and Stacey) The person who outperformed these four seasoned and well known comedians with decades of experience in film and television (and they were all excellent) was this guy. Phillip Seymour Hoffman At that point in his career Hoffman did not have the level of acclaim as he does now. He was mostly known for his eccentric supporting roles in mostly dramatic films such as Boogie Nights, The Talented Mr. Ripley, Happiness and The Big Lebowski. Just a year after starring in this zany comedy he played the role of Truman Capote in the the film Capote (2005), won the Oscar for Best Actor and from then on his status soared with him being called the greatest actor of his generation. It helped that his role was that of washed up actor Sandy Lyle who believes himself to be of the highest pedigree (despite never having a single role since a hit comedy in the 80s). Hoffman nails it with his character’s sometimes pompous, sometimes laidback mannerisms. He makes it seem effortless in that unique, low-key Phillip Seymour Hoffman style of his It's a pity that he died in 2014, at the prime of his professional career. He was finally being truly recognized for his talent and given leading roles. In my honest opinion, his performance in Doubt (2008) is without a doubt his greatest performance. I'm of the view he even outstaged Meryl Streep in their scenes together. I would've loved to see him take on more comedic roles. I think that he put his heart and soul into his performances and added his own subtle nuances to his characters. Even if you are like critics and don't think much of Along Came Polly, it's hard to hate Hoffman's unforgettable performance as Sandy Lyle.

What Scorsese film would have been better if directed by Spielberg and vice versa? Interesting question. In regards to Spielberg doing a Scorsese film, I know I may be in a minority but I never had much love for Scorsese's Gangs of New York (2002). I've never been able to sit through the entire film. In my honest opinion, just because the epoch the film is based on is an ugly period in history, it doesn’t mean that the film has to be inherently ugly. In the comparable and far superior Once Upon A Time in America (1984), Sergio Leone captures the pockets of childhood innocence and warm camaraderie in a truly poetic manner despite the inherent ugliness of the period documented. In Gangs of New York everywhere looked like a filthy trash heap. All the main characters were assholes. Everyone was somehow dressed in the most rattiest rags they could find. I think Scorsese was a little heavy handed in demonstrating the chaotic grittiness of the period. With the exception of Daniel Day Lewis the entire cast gave mediocre performances. The colours and camera work of the cinematography was glaring and unsettling and the whole revenge arc story didnt seem to have much of a point in the context it was used. In a nutshell the film was just a pointless, ugly film that just happened to have a measure of historical accuracy. Spielberg is the King of demonstrating the humanity that can be found in the absolute darkest periods of history. He does this without undermining historical accuracy or succumbing to fluffy melodrama. Of course the chief examples being Schindler's List and Saving Private Ryan. I think if Spielberg was given the job to direct Gangs of New York, the final product would've been a superior film with fleshed out, relatable characters, a better plot and overall a much more engaging experience for the senses. In regards to Scorsese doing a Spielberg film, I think the there is one film that was right up Scorsese’s alley that I think Spielberg’s did a disservice. Scorsese's eye for realism and portraying characters in their raw, unlikable form would've created a better product. No. It's not Munich (2005) It's Catch Me if You Can. The film was a the feelgood blockbuster movie of 2002. Frank Abagnale Jr was the antihero everyone couldn’t help but love, especially when portrayed by hearthtrob Leonardo DiCaprio. I enjoyed the movie when it premiered but it has aged poorly as of recently. Abagnale Jr was not just a scammer, it has been revealed that he is also a pathological liar. Much of the events described in his book are either grossly exaggerated or completely untrue. When you watch the film now you are treated to a self-indulgent, ego-stroking feast of fakery. I think Scorsese would've been a bit more skeptical towards the author's story and do the proper research into Abagnale Jr's life. The story would've been less attractive and a lot more cynical with moments of downright nastiness (very much in the vein of Raging Bull and The Wolf of Wall Street) but it might have been a compelling portrait of a fractured individual who thought more of himself than he actually was. It definitely wouldn't have the embarrassment that Catch Me if You Can suffers from today. So in conclusion, Spielberg and Scorsese should’ve simply traded director seats in the year 2002.

What is the weirdest thing you've ever witnessed a parent do? Neil was a troubled student in a school I worked in. Ms. Harris was his mom. In Trinidad we joke about the stereotypical ‘oppressed’ single mom who never sees wrong in her kids. The ones trying their best to raise their kids in a Government project, running out of the house delirious and screaming with curlers in their hair, desperately prostrating to the neighborhood to stop the awful policemen from arresting their innocent son who happened 'in the wrong place at the wrong time' during a robbery/breaking and entering. Ms.Harris was the textbook definition of such a mom; loyal to her children to the point of fanaticism and delusion. However, what set her apart from moms like her in the neighborhood was her gift for theatre. Ms. Harris could dish out so much pathos and could reach to the deep place inside her soul, channelling genuine emotions like the flick of a light switch. Those who didn't know any better would get easily influenced by her performances. She used this talent especially to bail Neil out of trouble. Once, Neil and a group of friends were to be expelled for selling marijuana on school premises. Before this was officiated, Ms. Harris came and gave an impromptu performance in the school staff room. ‘ ……go right ahead and tear the heart away from this poor, black woman. I have nothing. Neil has nothing. Only the love of struggling mother at wits end; a poor, black woman with no avenue in this world. Take my son and blind him so he cannot see the pain in his mother's face as we accept the fate of this cruel world; the fate of all poor, black women. As silly as her rhetoric was, she ended up getting her way and Neil and his friends had the matter covered up by the Principal and the police who witnessed this poor, black woman prostrating desperately towards them. One of the Literature teachers was so impressed that she approached Ms. Harris and told her that she belonged to a group that were looking for talent for the upcoming National 'Best Village’ competition sponsored by the Ministry of Culture. It was basically like a talent show with a focus on cultural dance, poetry, drama and spoken word. There were great prizes to be won and even if she didn't win, it would allow for great opportunities for her in local theatre. Ms. Harris agreed and immediately went and submitted an application for the audition. The event was scheduled the following month. Ms. Harris was dead set on giving the performance of a lifetime. She wanted the Minister of Culture to give her a standing ovation. She forgot all about Neil's problems at school to focus on her upcoming performance. She wrote an epic play that revolved around an oppressed woman who makes the journey to the motherland. There was to be a spoken word segment, a short play and end in a song and dance finale, complete with drums, dancers in exquisite costumes and professional lighting. However Ms. Harris bit off far too much than she could chew. Her obessesion with perfecting her vision of the performance led to many disputes with the dancers, sound effects, music and lighting personnel and nearing the date of the competition most of the crew quit and she was hard-pressed to find people to replace them. The day of the audition arrived and almost the entire neighborhood flocked to the Community Center to see Ms. Harris’ performance of a lifetime. Unbeknownst to Ms. Harris, the Minister of Culture was not going to be there, rather just a sole talent scout. There was no need for the amount of spectacle that Ms. Harris had in mind. When her moment came, she was nowhere to be found. Several people tried to contact her on her cell phone but she was not answering. Thirty minutes passed and the talent scout became furious as he had other locations to visit. Ms. Harris then materialized looking out of breath. En route to leaving she stopped the scout in his tracks to tell him that she was ready to perform but if only he could give herself and her dancers ten minutes to get their costumes ready and another ten minutes for the sound and lighting guys to arrive. The talent scout told her to perform now or she would be eliminated from the competition. Ms. Harris then began to prostrate in front of him saying: ‘How can you be so cold? How can you look at a poor, black woman and tell her that you are going to eliminate her? What has the world come to when a poor, black woman has a door shut in her face by a rich, black man? How can you? How can you?’ Needless to say the talent scout was not impressed by Ms. Harris' impromptu performance and had her eliminated. She learned the first lesson in Theatre 101 that day; don't overdo it

Would Hollywood actor Brad Pitt have made it in old or classic Hollywood back in the day? Very interesting question. For the sake of simplification let's just assume that by Classic Hollywood you mean the Hays Code era of Hollywood whereas sex, nudity, graphic violence, rape etc could not be demonstrated in Hollywood films. (1934 — 1968) 1930s — 1940s Hollywood Hollywood in the aftermath of the Great Depression and the outbreak of the Second World War. This is the age of the Go-Getter and although silent movies are now obsolete, it's exaggerative stage acting style is still rampant. Audiences of this era are favorable towards a certain type of male screen presence. Popular actors of the era are mostly an embodiment of what were considered desirable, manly traits. This is the era of Clark Gable, Cary Grant, Gary Cooper, James Stewart, Errol Flynn, John Wayne and Henry Fonda. The archetypal male film star was usually tall (over 6 feet), athletic, handsome, possessing a rich and resonant voice and possessing a certain self assured alpha male quality. The kind of man who would've made a great career as a top salesman or workforce motivator. The nation was wounded after two World Wars and these idealistic tropes were coveted by men and women alike. It was an age that was obsessively preoccupied with courage, persistence and survival. It was the era of sucking in your emotions and holding your chin high. Unless in possession of exemplary acting skills or song and dance expertise, actors who lacked several of these traits were relegated to minor supporting roles, comic relief roles, extras, stunt work or failed to make it in the film industry at all. Despite being ruggedly handsome, Brad Pitt would've had a hard time getting work in Hollywood during this era. He did not fit the height requirement, his voice would not be considered rich and animated and his brooding, sombre presence would've been a turn off for a national audience hungry for the next cocky, high shouldered, go-getting macho man. 1950s Hollywood The ideal aforementioned leading man is still prevalent with Charlton Heston, Gregory Peck, Burt Lancaster, and Rock Hudson maintaining the status quo. However standards are less rigid as actors like William Holden, Frank Sinatra, Kirk Douglas, Yul Brynner and Tony Curtis, who have the macho appeal but lack the height, are some of the top stars. A growing interest in brooding more sensitive type 'method' acting is gaining ground with the likes of James Dean, Marlon Brando and Paul Newman. Brad Pitt would've been better able to find work in such type roles but the competition would be fierce and only those with extensive stage experience and schooled in New York at the Actor's Studio would get top priority over some quiet, good looking guy from Missouri. 1960s Hollywood The growing counterculture revolution is finally making an impact on Hollywood. While the war scarred older generation is fading to make way for the Baby Boomers, the conservative values and ideal macho leading man is no longer as appealing for those hungry for emotional catharsis. The audience is yearning for a leading man who they could relate to, who shares their flaws and can demonstrate vulnerability. Even the more macho type actors are expected to demonstate weakness and more sensitivity. These would include Clint Eastwood, Sean Connery, Charles Bronson, Steve McQueen, Robert Redford, George Kennedy and Rod Steiger. Slurred speaking (Marlon Brando), meek voiced (Eastwood) overweight (Steiger) and short stature (Bronson) are traits no longer shunned by Hollywood elite. Brad Pitt would've found the greatest chance of obtaining prominent roles during this era. Who knows he might've even replaced Robert Redford in Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.

Do you feel uncomfortable at work around certain co-workers? If so, why? There’s a running joke on online chat-rooms and forums about people who look like created players. If you are/were an avid gamer you would get the joke instantly. If you aren’t then a created player is when gamers have the option of creating their own customized player i.e. choosing their skin colour, height, hairstyle, weight, clothes etc. Many gamers attempt to make the most random or disturbing looking player possible just for kicks e.g huge head, clown hair, wide apart eyes, inhuman skin tone etc. In the real world, it’s hardly likely you would come across anyone looking like these guys anytime soon but on the rare occasion that you do, you tell yourself, ‘Hey! That guy looks like a created player!’ Frivolity out of the way, there’s a man in my workplace who is like a created player. He’s not eerie looking but he is eerie in that no one can could put a finger on his personality without using the word ‘random.’ One day he would swagger to work looking as though he stepped off the set of a poor man’s Western movie, complete with snakeskin cowboy boots, cowboy hat, shirt opened up at the chest and RayBan shades (we work in a school by the way). Another day he would come dressed overly modest as though he spent the summer with monks in Tibet with a head shaved bald, large flowing shirt and giving an aura of calm resolve. Then another day would be a day of espionage as he would be dressed incognito and would spend the day peeping from behind a newspaper at God knows what. If you try to talk to him, you leave with a feeling of discomforting bewilderment. You would ask him a basic, ‘How did you spend your weekend?’ and he would start talking about why every teenager nearing adulthood should practice Feng Shui. Or He would come to you with an angry rant about why he will not teach any unvaccinated students while he himself isn’t vaccinated and hardly wears his masks. Or He would speak ill of teachers who come late to school while he himself has an abysmal regularity and punctuality rate. Everything about him is just random and contradictory. No one knows what he’s up to where he came from and where he’s going. But for me, though it’s uncomfortable to communicate with him, it’s fun to see the ultimate, living breathing created player.

What is your most interesting encounter with the police? I was working pizza delivery some years ago. I had a delivery to make at what is called ‘the old airport.’ It is a collection of buildings located at what used to be the official airport of the country some decades ago but has long since been discontinued since a more modern airport has been built nearby. As such the ‘old airport’ is now used to house a few airport related businesses and airport administration. It is rather a quiet, relatively vacant area in comparison to the actual airport and no one pays it any mind except for the people who wait for the bus there. One afternoon I dropped off a pizza to a lady who worked at the local Swissport that was located there. While riding the motorcycle out I was stopped by a police vehicle. The driver beckoned me to come over. The glass of his vehicle went down revealing a middle aged male officer behind the wheel and an attractive young female officer at the passenger’s side. The male pointed to some arrows on the surface of the road. Apparently I had entered along the exit arrow and was leaving along the entrance arrow. It was a really petty issue. Nobody cared about those arrows since the old airport was no longer in use and hardly any vehicle ever came there to begin with. Regardless I apologized to the officer and explained to him that I never noticed those arrows until now. Expecting him to let me off the hook and return to my duty I stood in silence waiting. ‘License and insurance,’ he then says in a stoic tone. ‘Is this guy for real?’ I thought to myself. I went to my wallet for my license and while searching I heard the guy explain haughtily to his female sidekick how he busted a pizza delivery man who didn’t even have a driver’s license but was working delivery and how he believes that regular check ups like this reduces the amount of accidents that occur on the road. From the tone of his voice I could sense that the man was trying to make some kind of impression on his female partner and that she was on some kind of training with him. Looking at her face I could sense that she was quite fed up the partner she had been assigned to for the day but was trying to be patient with him. I showed the officer my license. ‘And the insurance?’ Never in my years of working delivery had an officer ever asked me for insurance. The restaurant I worked for was a major chain and police generally knew that this franchise did not make joke with their insurances. Regardless I showed him the insurance title taped inside the back of the delivery box. ‘What’s this? What’s this?’ the officer bellows. ‘All insurances must be presentable for officers to inspect.’ The officer demands that I yank it off from the back and hand it to him. Another petty call. I pulled it off from the box and handed it to him. Meanwhile he barely looks at it but begins to chastise me about how dirty my bike looked and that I should be more prideful of my duty when delivering people’s food and how people die from food poisoning every day. He saw that I had another order to deliver. I was expecting him to send me on my way. This had gone on long enough. ‘What’s in that bag there?’ ‘It’s another order.’ ‘I know!’ he bellowed, ‘What is it?’ Did this man really want me to call out the order that someone made for a pizza? I explained to him it was a pepperoni and pine pizza. ‘Are you sure?’ ‘Yes,’ I replied and I was about to show him the customer’s bill when he said, ‘Take it out the bag and open the box.’ At that point his partner had had enough and she cried loudly, ‘Curtis are you some kind of ass?’ She folded her arms in defiance and shook her head. There was a silence and Curtis the officer proceeded to awkwardly laugh off the situation. ‘Pizza man,’ the officer said in a tone that showed a measure of humility, ‘Pay attention to the road. Don’t let us have this conversation again.’ With that said Curtis the officer returned to his vehicle. His female sidekick gave me an apologetic look with eyes that seemed to say ‘Believe me, you don’t want to be in my shoes right now’ and with that they were gone. I drove off myself, wondering where exactly Curtis was going when he asked me to open the pizza box. Did he expect me to have a stash of cocaine hidden there? Did he want me to try and bribe him by offering the pizza? God alone knows.

Why would I kill a mugger in self-defense? Are my valuables worth more than their life? I’ve been mugged four times. Two of these muggings were violent. In these muggings I had my face punched relentlessly. I had a beer bottle smashed on my head, requiring stitches. I had a gun pointed at my face. I got my pants and underwear torn open and had to walk to the police station afterwards with my junk in my hands. In both muggings I got laughed at by the muggers. I’ll never forget the moment when one of the muggers looked at me sitting defeated on the curb, robbed, bleeding and beaten. I’ll never forget how in the silence that followed he looked me in the eyes and growled ‘That’s how it is.’ In that situation I’m certain that same mugger would’ve killed me if needed. I felt a deep cynical hatred in him; that beating me to a pulp satisfied some inner rage he compartmentalized towards society. No. It wasn’t just about the money for them. They felt the world owed them something that they themselves couldn’t fathom what. What is it that I had that was so valuable to these muggers? In total I lost around $300 TT (43US), a cheap cell phone and wallet with my identification cards which would’ve been no value to them. Someone who so callously and casually engages in theft while inflicting violence upon his victims is someone who has agreed that they do not value your life nor theirs. Why must I pay special consideration to their lives while being beaten senselessly or having a knife or gun pointed at me? Does the small amount of money lost bother me? No. What bothers me is the reality that there are some people out there who saw me like garbage and inflicted a hateful beating while threatening my life, knowing fully well that the loot probably wasn’t worth it. My valuables may not be worth more than a human life but if in self defense I had fatally shot my armed and/or violent mugger, I would not be sending flowers to his family nor showing up at his funeral, nor would I suffer any sleepless nights over it. As the old folks in Trinidad love to say; how you make your bed is how you lie on it.

What's the most ridiculous thing a coworker told on you to your boss for? At my very first job at 19 years old I was a warehouse attendant. I was a naturally friendly individual and honestly believed that it was my duty to try and befriend all of my coworkers on my first day of work. I wore glasses and have pretty bad eyesight. I had a talk with a guy named Duane. He wore thick glasses also and looked and acted exactly like Big Smoke from the video game Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. I confided in him that my I was due for an eye test for new glasses. Duane had a ‘gangsta’ ideology about himself that made me feel awkward but I honestly believed I made a friend that day. His large, stocky friend Arnold who was even more provocative and blunt asked me to borrow $20 to buy lunch. I loaned him the money and humbly asked him to repay me the next day as I was low on cash. The following day I approached Arnold to get my $20 back because I needed it to buy lunch for myself. Arnold gets angry and makes a scene. He says that I'm trash because it hasn't even been 24 hrs and I'm harassing him for a measly $20. Duane chimes in and agrees with Arnold and chastises me for not understanding 'the game.’ Regardless I get my money back. An hour later the supervisor calls me in his office. He sits me down and tells me that he heard that my glasses are in need of a new prescription and that I have to get them changed according to Occupational Health and Safety law. I asked the supervisor if Duane told him this and he replied yes. The supervisor tells me that he's giving me a week to get proper prescribed glasses. I approached Duane and asked him why did he tell the supervisor something which I confided in him. I spoke in his language and asked him why he snitched on me. Duane replied that I crossed his boy Arnold by embarrassing him for the $20 he owed me so I qualified for being snitched on for my outdated glasses. Then there was silence. Such was the way of the gangsta. Duane snitched on my outdated glasses because I upset Arnold for publicly asking for my $20 back.

What should I absolutely not do when visiting your country? TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO Avoid hiring 'local tour guides.’ Stick to official touring groups from your hotel or large hiking groups. You’ve come to Trinidad on a vacation but you don't want to be so 'touristy.’ You don't want to sign up for the generic cross country tour the hotel is offering. You don't want to be crammed in a bus with a bunch of khaki short wearing, middle aged couples who want to stop the bus every 10 minutes saying. 'Hey driver, look there's a natural spring there. I want to fill my water bottle.’ Or 'Ooh driver stop the bus. I want to get a picture of those local Trinidadian cows.’ And you definitely don't want to go on the same well beaten hiking track where ten buses like yours are parked so more tourists like yourself could commence on a 5 minute hike, past dozens of souvenir stalls, to see a dormant mud volcano which, if you're lucky, might belch out a nauseating scent of rotten eggs. It sounds awful but believe me the other option is far worse. You'd meet someone who'd tell you, 'I know a guy who does private tours. He'll take you to the real hidden sites that the tour groups don't go and he's very knowledgeable of history and professional. You don't have to stick with the dull tourist tours.’ You want to make the extra effort and discover the hidden Trinidad (or Tobago) and this guy sounds like the real deal. Here are the problems with that offer: Discovering a makeshift stone axe . My Scottish cousins realized this too late when they hired some guy who was a friend of a friend of friend who did private tours. He was taking them to Turure Water Steps which was indeed a beautiful place with four amazing waterfalls, each bigger than the last. When I heard he was charging $1000 TT (roughly 150 US) to take them there I protested and told them that they were being ripped off. Anyone could take them there for free. They argued that he was a professional and had deep knowledge of the history of places. I went along with them for the trip. Some hours later, returning home, they agreed that they were ripped off. In summary the lesson learned here is that there are several people like that so-called tour guide who wants to rip off hapless tourists. Either you stick with your hotel tour or if you want to go off the beaten track, join a professional hiking/tour group or go with a large group of friendly, trustworthy locals. Doing otherwise could have you ripped off or even worse. Edit 31.08.21 Had no idea this little tidbit of info would've garnered so many upvotes. Thank you all for the support. Here are some more images of Turure. If you enjoyed this I can assume that you enjoy travel. Check out my piece on the island of Dominica, a pristine, little island lost in time. Click here.

What's the best "tourist trap" you've ever fallen into? Personally I've never fallen into this scheme but whenever I visit our tiny sister island of Tobago I roll my eyes seeing the amount of tourists who get caught in this trap. Imagine this… You’re on vacation with your family in the Caribbean island of Tobago, known for its stunning blue beaches and laid-back, bohemian lifestyle. As many tourists do, seeing that it's the closest beach to the airport, they spend their first day on Store Bay, the most commercially popular beach in Tobago. As you arrive down the steps, past all the numerous souvenirs, handicraft and food stalls, you look for a nice shady area on the sand to lay your beach towel and make camp. Unfortunately all the good spots are taken so you whip out that suntan lotion and decide to take in some Vitamin D because you'll be taking a dip in the water anyhow. Suddenly a sinewy barechested young man looking like this: Comes with a beach umbrella, and while taking puffs of his marijuana spliff, he stabs the umbrella into the sand amongst you, which provides much appreciated shade from the enhanced Vitamin D plus sunrays that are making you sweat. You think, 'Wow, what nice thoughtful people these Tobagonians are.’ You thank him but he doesn't seem to hear you. He leaves and you assume that the umbrella is complimentary of whatever tourism board is running the country as you notice practically everyone has an umbrella like yours. The man returns with a couple of beach chairs. You jump up ready to assist this helpful man. His mind seems distant as he stares towards the sea horizon as though expecting something. You say thanks again but he leaves without a word. You enjoy yourself in the sun and sea, taking a few splashes in the azure waters. Discussing plans for the evening with your spouse, watching the kids frolic on the sand. An old boat adorned in bright colours arrive on shore blasting music from its speakers. You see a bunch of people get up and head towards the boat. It's apparently a glass bottomed boat that tours the nearby beaches. The man magically appears behind you. ‘Yuh wah go on de glass bottom boat?’ he says. You take some time to translate his sentence and you quickly say yeah. He whips out a card of tickets and a pencil and writes a note under some tickets. He then leads you and your family to the boat and assists you all in helping climb onto it. What great hospitality! What great people! What a nice country! They really do go above and beyond for the tourists. These are the thoughts you think whilst enjoying the tour, staring at the beautiful sights while the children look at fishes and coral through the glass bottom. The tour lasts about two hours and when you return you decide that you will stay on the beach for the sunset. When the sun sets most people are leaving and you see your man along with others like him collecting their vacated beach chairs and umbrellas. You watch the sunset and fall in love with the country. Your man is somewhere behind you smoking another spliff and enjoying the sunset with you. However he seems to be scowling. You tell yourself that maybe that's just his countenance. Never judge a book by its cover. You decide to wrap things up and as you and your family assist in dusting off the beach chairs and folding and the umbrella, your man comes over with a few shirtless friends and takes over that duty. He is staring at you and you don't know what to say. 'Thank you for everything,' you say awkwardly, 'You've been so kind…..What's your name?’ 'Yuh have $1200 (TT) dollars for us sir.’ he says in a gruff, solemn tone while staring you in the eyes. His friends are poised nearby smirking at the scene. 'You didn't tell me you were charging me all this time! You didn't tell me the cost?’ You look at him and his men who look agitated and upset and you look nervously at the near deserted beach. You know that quarreling over money with a bunch of unknown, sinewy shirtless locals would not be a good idea given the circumstances. 'Brudda, if yuh don't mind’ said one of his friends, 'We real busy. Y’all went overtime. Jus pay we for our services nuh.’ He is saying this more as a growling threat than a request. You do your calculations. $200 US should cover the fee and give you back a little more than $100 TT change. You grudgingly give him the money. He looks at it, pockets it and he and his men leave without a word, laughing at something they were discussing, not even considering your change. You've just been schemed my good friend. Lesson #1 in coming to Tobago as a tourist. Absolutely nothing is free. Edit: Did not expect this little gem of advice to take off so quickly. But please be aware that these sort of schemes and unwholesome attitudes are mostly prevalent at Store Bay. The rest of Tobago is very easy going and trustworthy. The Government is doing its best to curb these type of characters from tainting our image. This is just a lesson to be on the alert if you do decide to visit our marvelous country. Edit 9.01.22: Those guys who try to scheme you with their beach chairs and boat rides in Tobago are nothing compared to the ‘trailer trash' of Trinidad. Click here to read all about it.

What screams "I'm pretending to be upper class"? My cousin David lived for two years in Trinidad after his upper-middle class parents decided to return to their homeland to retire. David did his SATs at ISPS (International School of Port of Spain), a school which caters to mostly foreign upper-middle/upper class students. It was there that he befriended Carlos. Carlos was a Venezuelan who had an immense stroke of luck. Carlos came from a very poor family in Venezuela and was said to be adopted on a charitable impulse by a rich Texas oil man. Carlos’ foster father didn't intend to have much of a relationship with him but rather wanted to make a point of turning Carlos' life around. He shipped Carlos off to Trinidad and ISPS and left with him a sizable monthly allowance to finish his SATs and pursue a college degree. It was there that Carlos met my cousin David. David did not like Carlos in the least bit. Carlos was the biggest show-off/braggart at ISPS. His first action upon being set to his own devices was to rent a furnished luxury apartment in Goodwood Park (the Beverly Hills of Trinidad). With this apartment he gained fame for hosting weekly parties for his fellow schoolmates laden with weed and alcohol. Like most of Carlos' ‘friends’ David befriended Carlos solely for the opportunity to be invited to these parties. Carlos' attendance at school and his grades soured but he didn't care. He took out a Range Rover and after a drunken night racing along the North Coast he crashed the vehicle and had it wrote off. It was a miracle that he survived and ought to have been an epiphany to change his ways. He didn't. His two years in ISPS were spent indulging, fraternising, boasting, drinking, smoking, chasing girls and maintaining the image of being the most popular student at ISPS. He wasn't the most popular. He was the most infamous. It was hard to find someone who truly liked him. I would include myself in that category. Once when I was in a restaurant with David, Carlos and a few of David's friends, I realized that I had no money for a meal. I made a joke about it. I told everyone that I would be taxing everyone 5% of their meal for charity as I was broke at the moment. Everyone laughed except Carlos who stared at me in horror as though I cursed God and my mother in one sentence. ‘Don’t go anywhere if you don't have any mah-nee!’ Carlos admonished towards me in a stern Venezuelan accent. It was strange how he was so deeply offended by someone near him making a joke about not having money and begging. Everyone stopped laughing. David paid for my meal making sure Carlos didn't notice. Carlos graduated with failing grades and soon found that his funds were depleted. He would guilt trip several of his ‘friends’ for lodging, reminding them of all that he lavished upon them. He reassured them that his foster father was going to send for him to return to the US. This of course was discovered to be a lie, his foster father had washed his hand of an adult Carlos. He found himself broke and homeless. Carlos still lives in Trinidad. He works an ordinary job and rents an unimpressive furniture-less apartment that is above his means. To this day he still brags about his brief period of wealth. His former colleagues take great pains avoiding him whenever they are aware he is around. Otherwise he would stop them in their tracks to entertain lengthy one-sided discussions about the good old days and would inveigle them to grab some drinks in a fancy pub in which they would listen to his ridiculous plans to score big, be constantly reminded of how much he did for their enjoyment at ISPS and then be forced to pay for the bill that he ran up but can't afford with the promise that ‘Drinks are on me next time amigo.’ Such is the life of Carlos. So to answer the question ‘What screams "I'm pretending to be upper class?”’ People like Carlos.

What movies can you watch all the time and never get tired of watching? Without a doubt Dirty Rotten Scoundrels (1988) is the movie I’d take with me to a desert island. I don't think the movie gets a fraction of the praise it deserves. I think it's the highlight of the careers of both its leads Steve Martin and Michael Caine. I must've seen the movie over 20 times and still it is a delight to sit and watch for its entirety. What makes it endearing as compared to great movies that you only watch once is that it doesn't take itself too seriously. There is no moral or lesson to be learned here. Two dirtbags, one a petty hustler, the other a gentlemanly con artist, make their living by manipulating wealthy, slow witted women. They make a bet as to who would be first to con a simple but good natured soap heiress who just arrived in the village at the French Riviera. What makes this film so rewatchable is that, yes it is silly movie, but it is also a very well written, well executed and thoroughly refined silly movie. The location and cinematography is absolutely gorgeous. The score and soundtrack is a fitting blend of waltzy French classical and sophisti-pop. Mostly filmed on location at scenic locations along the French Riviera, the film is one of the most gorgeous movies I've ever seen. From the beginning Villefranche-Sur-Mer train station to the breathtaking Beaulieu-sur-mer to the lookout at Villa Hier at the end, the film is a feast for the eyes. Not to mention the performances. Both Caine and Martin give stellar performances from a remarkably clever script but Martin steals the show and makes the character Freddy Benson his own in a highly physical role the likes of which only Martin can accomplish. Props also to Glenne Headly who plays mutual target of the leads, demonstrating an innocent charm that wins over the hearts of the conmen and the audience. The film takes a not so pleasant topic and turns it into a rather good natured, comedy film. If it were remade today it would be chocked full of the gratuitous profanity, nudity and sex that is the hallmark of modern day ‘comedy.’ There's not a single F-bomb, nor a sex scene, nor a gratuitous flashing of breasts etc. Frank Oz uses no cheap gimmicks to entertain an audience and as such the film can be enjoyed by the entire family. Watching Dirty Rotten Scoundrels is such a pleasure that watching it feels like a little vacation rather than a movie. I watch it every year as a sort of ritual and I am yet to find another movie that is such a timeless delight.

What is an example of an album that, in your opinion, was ruined by the producer and/or the production? It always blows my mind why no one mentions how awfully inconsistent the sound is in Jimi Hendrix's legendary Are You Experienced album. Not saying that it's a bad album, it's one of the greatest albums on Earth. However I can't help but shudder when I hear sound inconsistencies and downright amateurish recording. It's so sad that someone like Hendrix who was possibly the greatest guitarist of the 20th century had his masterpiece recorded in mono. His complex arrangements condescended to just a flat block of sound. Worse yet, because of financial burden, Chas Chandler, the producer and member of The Animals, had the album recorded in 16 different sessions at 3 different locations. When you go from track to track you can hear the chaos behind the production. Songs like Manic Depression, Stone Free and May This Be Love sound hollow as though recorded in someone's basement whilst Fire, Purple Haze and Hey Joe are treated with tender loving care. Love or Confusion sounds as though Chandler was tripping acid while recording and simply toying with the mix as within a few seconds the volume suddenly increases in itself erratically and from then on it's a brawl between guitar, bass and drums. In many instances the Hendrix's voice and guitar overwhelms Mitch Mitchell's drums and Noel Reddings bass. As much as I love Hendrix and his guitar prowess, he wasn't the greatest of vocalists and some tracks could of benefitted with greater accentuation of his talented bandmates. All in all, the chaotic production behind Are You Experienced makes it feel more like a collection of B sides (exceptional B sides) rather than a work of art. Each track takes me to a different place, but not in a good way. I'm sure this wasn't the ‘Experience’ Hendrix wanted the world to have, but say what, it's still an excellent album.

Whom did you feel bad for in high school? Balram. There was a boy who came from the depths of poverty named Balram. He was sinewy and had coarse skin and features that made him look like he jumped out of the pages of our history books as an indentured laborer from colonial times. Everything about him was out of sync with the rest of the class. This was the late 90s and baggy pants were the thing, Balram wore his khaki trousers wrapped tight around his skinny legs. Perms from excessive hair gel (my specialty at the time), corn-rows, Caesar styled and spiky hair was the rage amongst teenage boys back then. Balram wore something that looked straight out of a an old Amitabh Bachchan movie from the 70s. Balram's school uniforms always looked faded and threadbare. Never once did anyone see him wearing new items of clothing. This led to many of the kids in class poking fun at the possibility that Balram's family got used clothes for him. Balram didn't have cable. It was possible he didn't have a TV. Balram didn't care for the music everyone else listened to. He didn't go to the arcade and play video games. He didn't get excited hearing about Stone Cold Steve Austin. He was odd in that he only enjoyed games that demonstrated his eerie strength and his skills in survival. This included holding breath competitions, arm wrestling, 'mercy’ and 'bokee' (hitting an opponents fist by flicking a finger against it until someone gives up in pain). He didn't have much of a sense of humour. He would sit in class like an old Native American chief, peering knowingly at the world through his squinted, Charles Bronson-esque eyes while everyone else made jokes and acted like morons who needed attention. My friends and I would hang out with him but for some reason he never was an official member of our group. He preferred to roam alone. Once, I was tricked by some boys into pretending to want to beat him up, all for kicks. Before I could say 'Hey' Balram lifted me into the air by the shoulders and against the wall until I yielded. It was an impressive display of brute strength that I could never forget. In moments of boredom Balram was usually an easy target for jokes and insults. Some of the girls were particularly mean to him. One would say to that she would never be with a boy like him who looks dirty and always smells like old curry. The boys would always joke around that he came from 'the bush’ and came to school swinging on vines like Tarzan. One of the boys even managed to create a comic depicting Balram's life in the bush, fighting snakes and tigers on a daily basis etc. Balram learned to laugh with everyone and not let it get to him. In Form 3 Balram vanished. Always a recluse he never communicated to anyone what were his plans/intentions. Some months later he visited the school wearing a new uniform and with a friend at his side. He got transferred to a school closer to home where more rural kids like him were around. He looked much happier and was far more social than he was before. That day, most of the class ignored him but my friends and I held a reception to commemorate the good times we had with him. He said his new school was the best; teachers were hardly there and the kids did what they wanted. He showed me a tattoo that he got on his arm of a dragon. Even though the tattoo looked ridiculously amateurish and his clothes were still faded and threadbare and his hair still outdated my friends and I sang his praises and gave him his day. He really was a great guy. He had no fear of trying to fit in and had an infinite amount of patience for those around him. I wouldn't be surprised to find out that he made a huge success out if his life as an adult. But alas that day was the last time I saw him/heard anything about him.

Who are the most blatant examples of token black characters in TV and film? Hermes Conrad — Futurama I love Futurama. Unlike The Simpsons, Futurama didn't have a noticeable decline in quality for its later seasons. However two characters left a bad taste for me and would make me roll my eyes whenever they had any screen time. Hermes was one of them. He was so token, so uninspired that it was almost as though the writers just chose random character traits from a hat for the sake of having a black character. Uh……he's short…….and he's uh…….stocky and-and uptight…….and he's…..get this……. pedantically bureaucratic……..that's a winner…….and here's the final touch……..he's a Jamaican….yeah that's it. Aren't most Jamaicans like that? No they aren't. I'm not Jamaican but being from the Caribbean I find his portrayal pure cringe and borderline offensive. Firstly, his accent is atrocious. I've always liked Phil LaMarr from MadTV and as Marvin, the guy who gets accidentally shot in the face by John Travolta's character in Pulp Fiction. He's a funny, likable guy but that bootleg Jamaican accent he employed is almost blasphemous. Secondly, that unsavory shite rendered on top of his head that is supposed to be some sort of dreadlocks. Whoever designed him clearly hasn't been within 5 feet of an actual rasta in reality. What one thing did your father do that left your mother sobbing? Wasn't my biological father but my stepfather. Calling him 'stepfather’ is a bit of a compliment. He basically lived off my mom, was unemployed more often than not and barely provided anything for the rent free roof that lay above his head. Yet my mother persevered. She got involved with my biological father at a tender age and that relationship was traumatic due to his bipolar disorder. She was intent on having a proper family with my stepfather, especially after she bore him two daughters. As mentioned before he was more often unemployed and when when he did find a job it was temporary as he worked in construction. However, in the early 2000s he found some measure of success in the field and started getting established as a professional foreman. He got high paying, big contract jobs and had the power to hire and fire. Soon most of the guys in the street were given jobs by my stepfather and some of the neighborhood women sent love letters in the mailbox to my mother's ire. My stepfather would laugh it off. However as the months turned into years my mother calculated that with the amount of money my stepfather made, it wasn't reflected in the household. We were still broke, had almost no furniture, bills still piled up and the money he gave her was not any significant improvement to when he was roughing it. Things got worse when my stepfather would constantly disappear for the fortnight weekend, especially when he got his salary. When he gave my mother what scanty money remained in his wallet it led to ugly arguments. Everyone told my mother that my stepfather had to be seeing another woman. My mother refused to believe it. Instead she tried to nag, quarrel and harrass him into doing what was right and it just created more nasty arguments. She then resolved that he could no longer live with us but could see his daughters on the weekend. She believed this would change his ways. He readily agreed to this. One fateful Friday evening I was home and the phone rang. I answered it. I heard my stepfather's voice asking for 'Tracey.’ Tracey was the name of our neighbor's daughter. She was 24 years old and had a reputation. I said Tracey didn't live here. When my stepfather recognized my voice he immediately hung up the phone. My mother came and asked me who called. 'It's just S****n.’ 'What does he want?’ my mother said irritably. 'I dunno,' I replied, 'He just asked to talk to Tracey….I think he dialled the wrong number.’ At 16 years old I was a bit naive to comprehend what all this meant. However I'd never forget seeing my mother's face drop like she saw death materialize in front of her and later tears formed in her eyes. My stepfather was getting involved with our neighbor's daughter right across the street. That's where his money went. That meant everyone knew about it except her. That meant she was a fool. They parted ways permanently afterwards. My stepfather would demand that I say that I was mistaken. That it wasn't him who called. He's 68 now and his daughters want nothing to do with him. It really affected my mother as she became more withdrawn and a bit of a recluse and a hoarder. They both are barely on speaking terms. Sometimes I feel as though I should've had more common sense and just kept my mouth shut.

My girlfriend is mad at me for "not standing up for her.” She accidentally spilled her drink on a girl in the club. The other girl threw her drink on my girlfriend and her boyfriend shoved me. I grabbed my girlfriend and we left. What should I do? I love pub stories. I have one to share in a similar context. Years ago my friends from work and I would visit a bar that was pretty much a flashy looking dive bar. There was 6 of us. The biggest guy in the pack was Kurt who would always bring his wife (then girlfriend) with him. Curt is some specimen of human. If Dolph Lundgren discovered he had a secret Trinidadian half brother, I would gladly tell Dolph to come check out Curt. Curt is a bug dude. He’s so strong that once, three us at work in the warehouse wanted to play a prank on him. We wanted to restrain him on his forklift and bound him onto it with shrink wrap; keeping him there until somebody discovered him. The three of us combined could not subdue Curt and our prank failed. Curt has a great sense of humour when it comes to pranks but when it came to his wife's safety, all jokes ended there. So six us were in this bar taking turns shooting pool. Kurt and his wife were sitting on bar stools against the wall while the rest of us were around a pool table. Suddenly a sound of a beer bottle crashing onto the floor could be heard from the opposite pool table. A pudgy little manchild held his pool stick as though ready to fight someone. His drunken girlfriend released a cackling laugh and was making a poor attempt to subdue him. Apparently the pudgy guy was drunk and believed some guys outside the bar were throwing sweet words towards his woman. He broke his beer as a show of machismo towards the men outside and proceeded to hurl threats their direction Curt and his wife were laughing at something else at the moment. Pudgy guy’s eyes narrowed in on them believing them to be mocking him. He took his girlfriend's beer and hurtles it into the air where it lands and splashes beer upon them both when it smashes near their feet on the ground. Everything went silent. My friends and I at the pool table believed that this was going to be a brawl like no other. Pudgy guy had already provoked the men outside who seemed ready to thrash him and now Curt Lundgren was ready to give Pudgy a demonstration. However Curt is a smart individual. He recognized immediately what was going on and calculated the outcome. Three agitated men ready to fight outside the pub, one drunken idiot stirring up more trouble every second that passed and his girlfriend seeing the whole thing as a joke, broken glass everywhere. If Curt engaged in a fight things would get ugly and his wife could get seriously damaged. Instead Curt decides that we should leave. Without a word we headed to our vehicles and went home. Had Curt been alone he would given Pudgy what he deserved. However bar fights do not play off like they do in those 80s action movies. Everyone involved gets hurts and some even get scarred, maimed or killed. The bar has since closed down after the owner got killed in a drive by shooting last year.

I’m not in a position to judge who should and should not be parents but I would advise that one should defer from having kids if: If you fall in either of the above categories and also have the misfortune of having a difficult partner, prepare for one hell of a shitty ride. What has an employee said that immediately caused you to fire them? Jerome (not real name) was a new worker with a big mouth. He was 28 years old at the time, quite older than most of the guys he worked with like myself yet he acted, at best, like a spoilt 15 year old. He was always talking. He always had an opinion about something. He always had to question even the most simple orders and instructions. He believed himself to be the most intelligent person to ever walk the floor of the warehouse and always spoke at length of all the flaws he saw in our system and what he would do to fix the business if he were in charge. Our job was simple: a retail store wants products that we have, we go out with our grocery carts, pallet jacks, forklifts etc, get the products and have them packaged and ready for delivery in the morning. Not Jerome. Jerome's job was to distact you from what you were doing to talk shit about the company and how the money wasn't worth it. He would quote some nonexisting OSHA law that the company wasn't complying with and how he could sue the company if he wanted to. He would discuss his harebrained, get rich quick schemes that he never had to guts to actually attempt. He bragged about his family in the US waiting for him and how he didn't need to work himself like a slave for chump change like we did. At any given day he probably put out 20% of the output of the average worker. He was on a six month probationary period of which it would be decided whether he would be contracted as a permanent worker, given extended probation or let go. No one expected him to be permanently hired. Everyone basically tried to tolerate him for the six month probationary period as best as they could. However he started taking his shenanigans to the next level. He started making the (typically secluded) shampoos lane in the back warehouse his secret hideout. The lane was quiet, had no cameras and far away from our superiors’ field of vision. He decided to set up a makeshift man-cave behind a pallet of Tresemmé 2 in 1 Shampoo and Conditioner. There he would smoke, talk shit with the rare, harmless worker who came by for shampoos and he would watch rap music videos on his cell phone. At the month's end all warehouse workers were allowed to take from the damaged products. We had our own system of fairness whereby we rotated each worker to get a chance to get first pick among the damages. Jerome couldn't give a rat's ass about the system. During the third month of his employ it was observed that practically all of the best damaged goods had gone missing. A co-worker and myself smelt a rat in Jerome and we went to his man cave while he was on lunch and saw the damages were there hidden in boxes. We reported it to the supervisor who came and saw it. He held an emergency meeting and asked for the person who put those damaged goods in the back to come forward. Everyone eyed Jerome angrily but he remained silent. The supervisor reported the matter to the manager who reported it to the company owner and she immediately put a stop to the free damages giveaway. Now the anger towards Jerome had turned into a bloodlust. However the more angry everyone got the more lazy and defiant Jerome became. He was smart enough to abandon his man-cave after his attempted theft but he still spent more than half his working day loitering and talking shit. Every year the company paid for the company staff to have a party, usually at a classy sports bar or a nightclub. We all looked forward to it including Jerome who discussed at length his intention to get drunk off of free premium drinks and score with one of the pretty head office girls. However, one fateful afternoon the owner of the store had an impromptu meeting with everyone in the warehouse. She explained that the company decided to change the format of the staff party. She explained that it was expensive and inefficient having this party every year when too many employees ran up a bill drinking premium drinks all night and then not being able to come to work the following day. She gave the disappointing news that this time the party would be held at 12pm — 7pm the upcoming Sunday. Jerome released a snorting laugh while she spoke. Everyone in the warehouse went dead silent. No one had ever dared interrupt the owner, far less mock her. 'Excuse me,' she said, 'Is there something amusing?’ 'Nobody ever heard of a party 12 o clock in the afternoon,' Jerome said in his spoilt 15 year old voice. 'I've been to many parties 12 o clock in the afternoon' she replied. 'Yeah, birthday parties for kids' Jerome said smugly and looked about for someone to laugh but found only silence. The owner asked Jerome his name and how long he worked in the warehouse. Afterwards she continued her talk uninterrupted but after the meeting was dismissed she, the manager and Jerome went into an office for a talk. Some minutes later Jerome was seen leaving the compound, he was terminated from the job. Sad thing for Jerome was the owner apparently thought over what he said about the party and changed her mind about it. We were allowed to have our traditional, late into the night, party albeit minus the free premium drinks. We had a great time dancing the night away and toasting Jerome whose big mouth finally done some good for a change. Footnote 6/6/2023: There are a few commenters who seem to doubt the validity of my story on the grounds that 'so how come they didn't just fire Jerome as he's on probation?’ Probation is a process of testing and observing a new worker for short period. We signed a contract that we would be terminated on the grounds of serious offences like drug use, sexual harassment, assault, excessive absenteeism etc. Being a crappy worker and talking shit all day wouldn't get you terminated instantly but would definitely make you fail your probation and would have you under their radar for possible termination, which is exactly what happened in Jerome's case. Please. If you find all of this fantastic and unbelievable you are free to shake your head and scroll down.

Why is reading so important? Imagine this. You are with some friends on a fishing excursion in the Mediterranean sea. Miles away from the nearest harbor your yacht begins to sink. Who would you rather get help from? A) B) Another scenario. You are in a cabin in the Swiss Alps. An avalanche occurs and buries your cabin under twenty feet of snow. Your phone has enough juice to make one call. Who do you call? A) B) Final scenario. You have been drugged unconscious and abducted by traffickers who want to harvest your organs. Your kidnappers are taking you to a foreign land in which you cannot decipher the language, pinpoint the culture or recognize the terrain. Who would you rather get help from? A) B) If you chose ‘B’ for all the scenarios, congratulations, you are alive. If you chose ‘A’ for any scenario, you are most likely dead. The characters pictured under 'A’ are men who are extremely well-read. Ken Jennings — Record holder for the longest winning streak on Jeopardy. Karl Marx — Founding father of Marxism, a proponent of communism. Bill Nye — A mechanical engineer and popular television presenter, comedian and educator. The characters pictured under ‘B’ are men who are extremely well-read but also have a lot of worldly experience. Joseph Conrad — Polish born English author, explorer and ship captain. Jack London — American author, sailor, journalist and former Klondike prospector. Richard Francis Burton — English explorer, translator, linguist, historian and writer. This is not slight against the achievements of the characters under 'A’ it's just that the fellows under 'B’ have allowed for the knowledge they've amassed through reading to inspire them towards physical action which in turn develops experience and skill. Ken Jennings and Bill Nye might be able to tell you what is the distance of each planet in the Solar system from the sun in less than a minute but that doesn't mean NASA would aggressively pursue them. Marx, if he were alive, could write a 1000 page book on why he thinks 20th century communism failed but do you think Maduro or Castro would’ve employed him as an advisor? Group A are individuals of impressive intelligence but any logical thinking individual would recognize that Group B is superior in regards to worldly applicability. So to answer the question, reading is important to gain knowledge. Reading is very important, but not as important as the ACTION that it stimulates.

Which TV shows were popular when you were younger that would flop today? Why? Oh man. There are so many shows from the 90s that would flop hard had they been released (as they were) today. These two shows ruled daytime television for a long time in the mid 90s. I think one of the reasons for the success of the two interrelated shows is the fact that they were different and there was nothing else on. These weren't the days of Netflix, streaming, 4K/HD, watch at your own pace, high production value but limited seasons/episodes, hundreds of options to choose from high speed internet TV. These were the days of ‘Damn I missed my show’ cable television, paper TV guides, one new show every few months, low budget production with endless episodes and seasons etc. These were the days of ‘take what you can get’ on TV. HERCULES: THE LEGENDARY JOURNEYS Hercules is this chill, alpha-jock type guy who roams around New Zealand (wearing the same Super V-neck goatskin vest and tight leather pants every day) meeting nice quirky villagers of whom he saves from various villains ranging from petty con-men to full blown freakish monsters. At his side is a short, blond, surfer-dude like Iolaus who is the comic relief character. This is the premise for practically every episode. The show is supposedly set in ancient Greece yet don't be surprised to find English knights, Chinese peasants, Japanese ninjas, Nordic Vikings, Mongolian warlords, Egyptian Pharaohs or any cool and exciting historical anachronism discovered randomly during Hercules’ wanderings. The always well-shaved Kevin Sorbo would never break a sweat or mess up his lovely long hair in fights. Everything always worked out well in the end for Hercules, Iolaus and the villagers and if things got truly icky then you know it would take a second or third episode for the villain to be destroyed or for Iolaus/a love interest/a child to recover from near death. XENA: WARRIOR PRINCESS It’s pretty much the same thing except the leads are women. Xena (previously a minor Hercules villain on the show) atones for her past by going around saving helpless villagers with the aid of her short, blond quirky bard Gabrielle and the village idiot Joxer. Unlike Hercules, Xena had more personality and a rather interesting ‘Ay ya ya ya ya’ war cry accompanied with more of a focus on action scenes rather than Hercules’ constant spew of Dad jokes. The show became far more popular than its predecessor and ran from 1995 - 2001 whereas Hercules began in 1995 as well and ended 1999. Comparing these two shows with the crop of fantasy shows that are available now is definitely a chalk and cheese comparison. Take a look at the following screenshots. Now take a look at various people doing Hercules and Xena cosplay: You can barely tell the difference! Historically inaccurate clothing, easily accessible and cheap to film ‘forest’ backgrounds, pampered hairstyles, anachronisms galore, Hercules: The Legendary Journeys and Xena: Warrior Princess were nothing more than glorified cosplay. If either show were released today, as they were, they would be a source for ridicule and memes. However if I can give one positive comment for the show I would have to say that it doesn’t try to secretly force any message down my throat. Xena is a woman who kicks ass. She is not a feminist and definitely not a lesbian as that lame rumour suggests. Hercules doesn’t spout any subtle parables promoting socialism or taxing the wealthy. There is no powerful and evil villain that looks and acts like Trump (or Bob Dole to be more precise with the time). The show is silly and stupid and doesn’t promote any type of political activism. So I’d definitely watch Xena or Hercules over Rings of Power and She-Hulk any time, any day.

What was your mechanic scam that you caught that they never expected you to find? Some mechanics will charge you based on how you look/dress. Not a scam but rather a form of stereotyping. For a period in my life I worked two jobs. During the day I had an office job in a Ministry in the Government and during the evening I worked pizza delivery. I drove a beat-up, old pickup that was over twenty years old and looked it. At some point in time I was badly overdue in terms of an oil change. I had a decent mechanic, Doc, who would not only change my oil but also my air, fuel and oil filters AND fix any minor issues that needed attention. For all this he would charge $150 TT ($21 US). This was an exceptionally good rate compared to the price and quality of service I got from all the other mechanics. Sadly, Doc began having health problems and I was forced to look for a new mechanic. I was informed of a father-son mechanic team who were known for great service and affordable rates. I took some time off my office job and headed towards their location probably looking a lot like this: I was in some of my best threads, sporting a new haircut and pair of glasses, full of confidence and dare I say, looking quite dashing. I did not intend to impress the mechanics, I was not even aware of how I looked. I was simply having a good fashion day. I introduced myself to the mechanics and explained my situation. I gave it my all to be as friendly, polite and sociable as I could and even offered to help bring over tools for them as they worked on my vehicle. During all this time I couldn't help but notice they were being rigidly formal and courteous with me, constantly referring to me as ‘sir,’ avoiding idle chatter and not showing any particular interest in me or my background. When they were finished, I went to the father mechanic and queried the cost. I was expecting $200 at most, maybe even as high as $250 seeing that they finished my job so speedily. However when I heard him nonchalantly mutter $500, my jaw dropped. ‘Five Hundred?!’ I cried, ‘How come so much?’ ‘We changed your oil, the air, fuel and oil filters,’ he explained lifelessly, ‘Aired your tires and eh…changed your gearbox and differential oil……that’s full service.’ ‘I didn’t want full service,’ I cried, ‘I just wanted my oil and filters changed.’ ‘Oil and filters changed?’ he replied almost stupidly, ‘That’s full service. Full service is $500. Isn’t that right Jason?’ He directed that question to his son who was in the process of jacking up someone’s car. ‘Yup,’ Jason replied monotonously without glancing, ‘Ask anybody here.’ There was a silence. I realized there was nothing I could do. I should’ve queried the cost before I allowed them to work on my pickup. I paid them their money and left, feeling thoroughly cheated and irritated, telling myself I would never do business with them again. Some weeks later I’m off to start my shift doing pizza delivery on a busy Friday evening. I’m nowhere near looking my best as I’m sporting a washed out and stained ‘Mario’s Pizza’ shirt, a beaten up red cap, a baggy and threadbare trousers and I’m in dire need of a haircut. My appearance was similar to the photo below but far more scruffy. I pressed on the clutch pedal, only to find that it was slow to rise up from the floor. Clearly my clutch had a bad fluid leak. If my vehicle broke down I would have to pay a fortune to hire a wrecker and quite possibly miss my shift. I saw that I wasn’t far from the father and son garage so I slowly guided the pickup into their compound. They saw me looking frantic and disheveled in my old pizza delivery clothes and immediately came to my assistance. I cut the pleasantries short and informed them of the clutch problem and how my manager would ‘have my ass if I took a day off on a Friday.’ They told me to calm down, that it wasn’t a serious matter. They began to jokingly tease me that they wouldn’t work on my pickup unless I brought a free pizza for them. They then proceeded to engage in idle chatter regarding fast food vs home cooked meals as they jacked up the pickup and put it on stands. I then realized that they didn’t recognize me with this shoddy uniform. They looked so much at ease and were so much friendlier than when I last visited them. Then the son got into his car, drove off and returned with a clutch slave cylinder and fluid and in two-twos they had my pickup back in order. I was quite impressed and grateful for the speedy service. However I cringed knowing that I would probably be slapped another $500 fee. I queried to the father mechanic as to how much my bill was and he said to his son, ‘How much you pay for that stuff Jason?’ ‘About two hundred,’ Jason replied. ‘Give us $250 pizza man. It’s your lucky day. Just make sure and bring us a pizza when you get the chance.’ ‘Of course!’ I lied. They barely charged for the labor. In fact they were much more fond of me as a salt-of-the-Earth, minimum wage earning, slave to the customer, regular Joe, plying his trade to make a living. They saw me as one of their own and extended a helping hand to someone who they believed roughed it out in life. Had they known that this was actually my second job and I had a comfortable office job in a Government Ministry, I would’ve seen a much different outcome. So I learned a decent hack in life when dealing with mechanics and various other tradesmen. I don’t work pizza delivery anymore but whenever I go to see those mechanics or go to meet plumbers, electricians, builders etc, I wear that old Mario’s Pizza uniform to counteract against their built in stereotypes. Doing this I find myself getting good rates, great service and making new friends much better than if I were wearing office wear and a fancy tie. C’est la vie! Edit 10.01.22. Those mechanics tend to scheme but you can find a way around them. They pale in comparison to the illegal scams some of our fast food restaurants attempt on a daily basis. Why is Eric Clapton such a highly rated guitarist when he's very average? Average you say? Clapton is in my personal top five of greatest guitarists. I'd even rank him higher than Hendrix and just a smidgen below Duane Allman. I dont know anything technical about guitars, I can't play and I definitely can't determine prowess. However I've listened to hundreds of guitar oriented albums and only a handful of guitarists stick out in terms of consistency of quality. Clapton is definitely one of them. For someone to listen to Disraeli Gears and call the stunning solos on that album average would be the rantings of a madman or the simply just a common troll. From his work with The Yardbirds, John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers, Cream, Blind Faith, Derek and the Dominos and his solo work (my least favourite, but heck he wrote Tears in Heaven) he has proven to be more than just average. I think the best performance depicting Clapton's talent is his guitar duel with The Band's Robbie Robertson for the The Last Waltz concert. Here one can see two immensely talented guitarists politely trying to upstage one another in a mastery of improvisation. The fans who wrote 'Clapton Is God’ on a London wall were not paid to do so. They did it because something about his guitar work touched them deeply inside that they felt him to be on a higher realm than ordinary people. Definitely doesn't fit the description of someone with average talent.
